keyFacts: The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony is being held at the Palladium Theatre in London, marking the first time the event takes place outside France to honor Stanley Matthews.

body: JUMP TO:
PALLADIUM THEATRE, LONDON — After a whole year of goals, trophies, speculation, and celebration, the time to learn the winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or has finally arrived.
Tonight, France Football will reveal the winner at the award gala, which has been won by four different players in each of the last four years.

For the first time, the ceremony will be held outside France, as they honor the first winner of the Ballon d'Or, Stanley Matthews, by holding the 70th trophy presentation at the Palladium Theatre in London, England.

Hosted by Kate Scott and Thierry Henry, this year's ceremony will reveal the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner for the men's and women's side, as well as a host of other awards including best coach, best goalkeeper, best young player, and best club.

articles.headline: Watch out, YouTube; Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
keyFacts: Instagram announced it is testing the upload of Features, which are videos up to 90 minutes long, marking a shift toward long-form content.
Instagram head Adam Mosseri and a Meta spokesperson said the platform is currently exploring monetization and advertising models for the longer videos.
Instagram is testing these Features and related tools in Brazil and a small U.S. test, while also working on improved discovery and TV app features.
body: If you could have one million followers on any social media platform, which would you choose? There is a correct answer, and it’s YouTube, assuming you’d like to get paid for your work. But Instagram’s latest update could upend YouTube’s long-held position as the most lucrative platform for creators, if only Instagram plays its cards right.

Instagram announced on Monday that it’s testing a new type of video upload that will allow creators to share “Features,” videos up to 90 minutes long. After years in which every social platform (even LinkedIn!) aggressively pursued short-form video, this is a notable shift in strategy for Instagram.

Short-form, vertical video content has defined the internet of the 2020s, but the creators behind these clips don’t actually make much money directly from platforms like Instagram — the Meta-owned platform has some monetization tools like subscriptions, but it doesn’t typically pay creators on a per-view basis.

“You can get paid by the platform directly, you can get paid by a fan, and you can get paid by a brand,” Instagram head Adam Mosseri explained on the Colin and Samir Show, an interview show about the creator economy. “And right now, the way that it works on Instagram primarily is you primarily get paid by brands. Some people get paid by fans. We have still a small performance-based program, but… we spend more money than we make back by a long shot, and so it doesn’t really make sense to scale up because we’re just burning capital.”

YouTube’s payment model is more straightforward: there are ads on videos, and creators enrolled in YouTube’s Partner Program get 55% of the ad revenue YouTube earns from their videos. That adds up. The platform said last year that it paid more than $100 billion to creators, artists, and media companies in the previous four years.

Instagram and TikTok haven’t been able to replicate YouTube’s model with short-form content, which is inherently trickier to monetize than longer videos because there’s less room to place ads. Many creators see those accounts more like promotional arms for their YouTube channels than meaningful drivers of revenue.

Instagram is encouraging creators to upload longer videos, as it already did eight years ago with the now-defunct IGTV. It’s possible that its parent company Meta, which makes its billions on advertising, will put ads in those long-form videos, too.
If Meta does add ads, could Instagram meaningfully compete with the YouTube Partner Program for the first time?

“It’s too early to share a long-term monetization model, but we’re exploring ways for creators to earn from brands, fans and Instagram, including performance-based incentives,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch. “Over time, we think there will be compounding benefits for creators to tell new stories, reach new audiences, and find new partners, which should lead to many monetization opportunities.”
It’s not a particularly promising answer, but it’s also not a “no.”
Mosseri explained in a video announcement why the platform is suddenly embracing long-form content after scrapping its old video product, IGTV.

“For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram,” Mosseri said, noting that shorter content like Reels drives more shares and DMs among users. Instagram VP of Product Tessa Lyons, who has been advocating for this change, finally convinced Mosseri to give long form another shot.

“Reels is still going to be a core part of Instagram. But when you want to go deeper with the creators you love and the content that they’re creating, you should be able to do that on Instagram,” Lyons said in the video.

In other words, Instagram would rather keep fans on its own platform to enjoy both short and long-form content from a creator than lose them to YouTube. Instagram is testing a feature called “Clips as Reels,” which lets creators make Reels out of their long-form content. The Reels link viewers to the longer video. Viewers can also save the longer video to send to the Instagram app on their TV.

Instagram is currently testing “Features” and “Clips as Reels” in Brazil, and will now expand to the U.S. in a small test, as well. The platform is also working on improved discovery features for Live video and a hub on a creator’s profile for episodic Reels, meaning a series of connected Reels similar to TikTok’s playlist feature.

“The thing that the team has been working on that we’re excited to share with you is trying to make it so that the short-form and the long-form video can be symbiotic,” Mosseri said. “We’re going to try to support these different types of formats, both in the mobile app, but also on the TV app, which I think is . . . going to take some time to get right. But I’m actually very excited about it, and we’re very committed to it long term.”

articles.headline: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse PSA: There’s An Easier Way To Fast Travel That The Game Is Not Good At Telling You About
keyFacts: Players of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse can fast travel between save-point mirrors by crouching in front of them.
The game fails to adequately explain this mirror teleportation mechanic to players.
Players discovered this feature independently, as the game's hint system does not clearly outline the method.
body: Are you overwhelmed by the sheer size of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse? Do you wish, as you travel the streets of Paris and Dracula’s Manor, that it was easier to return to specific, pinpoint areas? Do you wish you didn’t have to use The Ferryman’s fast-travel boat which will only teleport you to a general zone?

Have I got some good, possibly too-fucking-late news for you! You can fast travel between Belmont’s Curse save-point mirrors. All you have to do is roll up to a mirror, crouch down, and wait for Rose to teleport to the mirror world. There, you have access to almost every mirror you’ve unlocked within a specific zone and once you get to a certain story point, you can use it to travel from mirror to mirror throughout the entire game, cutting out The Ferry-middle-man.
And the game never adequately explains this to you.

One thing I appreciate about Belmont’s Curse is that there’s a robust diegetic hint system that tells you how to figure out your next objective. There are a handful of bonus bosses and other goodies not on the game’s critical path but getting to them isn’t straightforward, though the game is pretty good about dropping hints to help you find them. For example, the Mammon boss is hidden behind a door that’s only unlocked when you’ve collected three special items. Explore enough in the game, and you’ll find clues telling you where to look for those items. Another really cool use of diegetic clues that’ll help if you’re looking to 100-percent complete the game and don’t yet have the item that lets you know a secret is nearby: the map will tell you! A complete section of the map will have a brown background; any area where there’s still a secret waiting to be found will be purple.
BUT!

Sometimes I don’t want an in-game hint, I need to be told directly. Belmont’s Curse is so big and so much of it is optional that it’s easy to miss important things. I mean, I’m the one who blindly stumbled into the extra-bad ending because I got lost on my way to an early boss fight. (Ironically, I didn’t find the clue that tells you how to unlock the boss arena. Yes, this game is good with its hint system…sometimes.) I’m pretty sure the game leaves some kind of note cluing you in that you need to kneel in front of a mirror to unlock mirror-to-mirror teleportation fast travel, but I don’t think it should be too cute about something as critical as getting around a map that makes the Minotaur’s labyrinth look like a 30-square-foot Manhattan efficiency apartment. The only reason I found out about it at all was because my husband, who is also playing the game, stumbled upon it himself and let me know.

articles.headline: Mass Effect's Longshot #SaveMassEffect Campaign Actually Has a Chance
keyFacts: EA announced the closure of BioWare after 30 years, leaving the next Mass Effect game trapped in EA IP purgatory.
Devoted fans launched the #SaveMassEffect social media campaign and a petition that has already surpassed 200,000 signatures.
Voice actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, along with Owlcat Games, urged players to support the campaign to save the game.
body: On Oct. 21, EA officially announced the closure of legendary RPG maker BioWare after 30 years of operation. With the shutdown, the next Mass Effect game is now trapped in EA IP purgatory. But over the past week, devoted fans of the series have rallied around a social media campaign to save the game, fittingly called #SaveMassEffect. And even though it's one hell of a longshot, there's historical precedent for success here.

Mass Effect has had a tumultuous decade. In the early 2010s, the original trilogy earned its place as one of the best RPG space operas of all time, thanks to its well-realized sci-fi world, fascinating cast of characters, and emphasis on player choice. Its 2017 spinoff, Mass Effect: Andromeda, was more divisive; players loved the action, but didn’t click with the narrative or characters like they did with the original game. EA put Mass Effect on ice soon after.

In 2020, BioWare revealed a new Mass Effect game was in the works, and teased it intermittently over the following years. Some early promotional materials suggested it would serve as connective tissue between Andromeda and the original trilogy. Shortly after BioWare’s closure, a trailer for the next Mass Effect project, called Mass Effect: Universe, leaked online, teasing a radical departure for the series. Set 600 years after the events of the main trilogy, several people familiar with production likened it to “James Bond meets John Wick in space.” For fans of the series, seeing Mass Effect: Universe footage make the rounds only made its cancellation sting even more.

This entire situation smacks of another sci-fi masterpiece that was canceled before its time yet returned off the back of passionate fan outcry: The Expanse. Based on James S.A. Corey’s series of novels, The Expanse is set in the near future, where humanity has colonized the solar system. Fans flocked to its grounded approach to space opera, which focused more on roiling political tensions between interplanetary nation-states rather than fantastical sci-fi concepts and creatures that bordered on fantasy (cough: Star Wars, Star Trek, Dune).

In 2018, SyFy canceled its TV adaptation of The Expanse after three seasons. Fans immediately rallied around a digital awareness campaign, #SaveTheExpanse. IRL astronauts peppered social media with calls for its return. So did George R.R. Martin. But a few months later, Amazon picked up the show (founder Jeff Bezos, who announced its revival personally, was reportedly a fan), where it ran for three more seasons on Prime Video. Telltale Games released a video game prequel in 2023, and Owlcat Games is currently working on the spinoff The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, a promising third-person action RPG due out next year.

Over the weekend, the #SaveMassEffect campaign saw a similar tidal wave of interest. Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, who voice the female and male versions of protagonist Commander Shepherd, urged players to sign the petition. As did Owlcat Games, which noted how The Expanse was saved by fans years ago. There are even billboards in Times Square about it, Kotaku reported. As of this writing, the #SaveMassEffect petition has been signed by more than 200,000 people.
By the end of its run, the #SaveTheExpanse campaign ultimately accrued 138,420 signatures.
Of course, there are some notable differences between these two endeavors. Mass Effect is a video game. The Expanse is a TV show. Completely different worlds.

But you can nevertheless run the burn rate of what it would cost to see Mass Effect: Universe over the finish line. According to figures from Glassdoor, the average game developer salary in Edmonton, Alberta, where BioWare was based, is roughly $70,000 CAD (or $49,857 USD). Bloomberg reported that BioWare employed roughly 50 people at the time of its shutdown. Additional reports (albeit unconfirmed) suggested BioWare was targeting a 2028 release for Mass Effect: Universe, meaning two more years of active development.

All told, that comes out to roughly $5,000,000 of overhead — or about the cost of producing one episode of The Expanse during the SyFy days, according to one of its actors. (Amazon has never publicly revealed how much it cost to produce seasons 4 through 6 of The Expanse, but as any fan will tell you, there was an unmistakable uptick in production value between the SyFy seasons and the Prime Video ones.)

Of course, this napkin math leaves out one potentially enormous expense that could halt this entire thing in its tracks. As the original #SaveTheExpanse petition noted, Amazon already had U.S. streaming rights for The Expanse when it picked up the show. The rights for Mass Effect: Universe remain squarely in EA’s court. If EA doesn’t want to license or sell them, there’s not much anyone can do about that.

But on the other hand, it’s not like the Mass Effect IP is entirely immune to licensing: a show based on Mass Effect is still expected to move ahead despite BioWare’s closure. The company producing it? Amazon.

articles.headline: Texas Longhorns look for an answer to their third-quarter struggles in SEC play
keyFacts: Texas held halftime leads in all four of its SEC games but has been outscored 31-3 in the third quarter across those matchups.
Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said he plans to make subtle tweaks and changes to the team's halftime routine to fix the struggles.
Texas will play Mississippi State at home on Saturday for its next game.
body: Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian during a timeout against Mississippi Rebels in the fourth quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman)
During SEC play, Texas football often found itself halfway home to a conference conquest.
Texas 10, Tennessee 3
Texas 17, Oklahoma 7
Texas 17, Florida 10
Texas 24, Mississippi State 3

But as most football fans know, a game on the collegiate level lasts for 60 minutes so what the scoreboard says while the home team's band is performing at halftime isn't permanent. Those numbers are simply a placeholder.
MORE Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter

That has proven to be the case for Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC). Despite taking leads into the halftime intermission of all four of its SEC games, the Longhorns have lost twice and had their two wins come down to a last-second heave into the end zone.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom)
Why haven't all of these halftime leads translated into wins? Well, let's start with what is happening to the UT offense in the third quarter.

Over its four SEC games, Texas has been outscored by a 31-3 margin in the third quarter with those three points coming Sept. 26 at Tennessee . The Longhorns have averaged 0.8 yards over 30 third-quarter rushes - five of which were sacks - while UT quarterback Arch Manning has gone 10-of-20 for 103 yards. Texas had gained six first downs in those third quarters, punted 10 times and committed one turnover.

Are those numbers out of the norm? Overall, the Longhorns are scoring 25.5 points per game in conference play. Texas is averaging 3.5 yards over its 140 rushes - 15 of which are sacks - while Manning had thrown for 846 yards while completing 65 of his 100 passes. Mac Chiumento has punted just 13 times outside of the third quarter.
"We've just got to do our 1-11. If one thing goes wrong, you can see what happens out there," tight end Michael Masunas said.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning warms up before the game against the Mississippi Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman)
What adjustments are the Texas Longhorns making at halftime?
The Longhorns' second-half struggles might lead one to wonder what's happening in the Texas locker room during halftime. So what is happening in the Texas locker room during halftime?

Earlier this month, NFL quarterback Aaron Rodgers told reporters that halftime breaks for football players may not be what people envision . Sure, some adjustments are made and meetings are held. For the most part, though, players use the time to catch their breaths.

On Saturday, the 11th-ranked team in the Associated Press poll will play its third straight home game when Mississippi State (4-3, 2-3) comes to town. articles.headline: Ballon d’Or 2026: updates from 70th edition in London – live
keyFacts: Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Spain won the men's young talent of the year award for the third consecutive year.
Andriy Shevchenko presented an award and told attendees that talent provides opportunity, but hard work, discipline and self-belief remain essential.
Articles on the Ballon d’Or website lauding Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal appeared to leak ahead of the official results.
body: Lopez tells Henry and Scott she’s had a great year, and she has – again. So far, she’s the only player to have taken this award and, at 20, she’s scope to win another.
She then gives her mum a special mention,saying her presence is felt every day and it’s from her she learnt to fight and never give up. What a player she is, what a player she’s going to become.
Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Spain wins the men's young talent of the year award for the third year in a row
He’s grateful to win the award but feels his teammate, Pau Cubarsi, should be collecting this award. He thanks his teammates at club and international level.

Here comes Andriy Shevchenko, 2004 winner, to present the award, and he says the technology in the game has changed but one thing will never change: talent gives you the opportunity, but hard work, discipline and self-belief are essential.

“This, and Indeed many individual awards, can be easily fixed by making past winners ineligible,” writes Matthew Elliott. “Applying this rule to the Ballon d’Or would have rewarded not only Sneijder and Ribery, but Iniesta, Neymar, probably Luis Suarez, and plenty of others who deserve a spot on the podium.”
You had me until Luis Suarez, but yup, Wisden do this with their cricketers of the year and it works well. Anyroad up, Kate Scott and Thierry Henry have taken to the stage, so it’s on with the show.
OK, we’re ready go, so of course Jorja Smith is singing Blue Lights. On which point, Burna Boy is in attendance, though I’m not sure if he’s performing.

Bunny Shaw is in the house, and if it’s not her year this year, it might well be some time in the future. She might be the most natural goalscorer in the women’s game and says being nominated is a “wonderful feeling”, reward for all her hard work.

“You quote Josh Goldblatt,” begins Craig Reeves. “‘How many of these candidates actually make you smile for the quality of their football and skills?’” wonders Josh Goldblatt. “‘Maybe Lamine, but the last entertainer surely was Ronaldinho, 2005 winner.’”

“Why does it feel like these days most ‘football fans’ don’t actually like football? If you’re not entertained by Harry Kane’s quality, I’m afraid you’re watching the wrong sport. Maybe try basketball? (And I’m an Arsenal fan, so there’s no bias here!)“

I don’t think the point is that Kane isn’t entertaining, but he’s not an entertainer, per se, but an accumulator. Similarly, post-2006-07, Cristiano Ronaldo changed from entertainer to accumulator, but he was still entertaining thereafter.

Caroline Graham Hansen also hasn’t prepared a speech, which is probably OK, brilliant though she is. I wonder, though, if we might be seeing her again next term, now Alexia has left Barca and there’s more room for her to be the star.
Lamine Yamal has arrived, and as he walks through the vestibule there’s a minor scuffle with a cameraman and security. I think we’ll need a replay there, but doubt Dazn oblige us.

“So, ‘Denis Law was a penalty-box player …’” begins Geoiff Wignall. “What? He was a No 10 who played (superbly) as a striker for the sake of the team and not so much a box to box player as byline to byline. Not many could pass the ball around Pat Jennings from 18+ yards.

Likewise Greaves was also a 10 - and his international goals to games ratio is still better than Kane’s, without such a percentage of penalties or games against minnows. I don’t seek to disparage Kane, fine player that he is (if prone to gamesmanship), just to set the record a little straighter.”
Denis Law a no 10? I’ve never heard such thing before. Here, in Richard Williams’ obituary, we see the words “penalty area” in both the first two paragraphs.
Between 1962-63 and 68-69, he scored 29, 46, 39, 24, 25, 10 and 30 goals. That is never a no 10.

What Kane said about how his teammates talk about him – what a feeling that must be. During the World Cup, it was moving to hear the England players discuss his dedication, seriousness and intensity in every single training session, and their desire to learn from him; no one has done more to maximise their talent.

Kane says he’s a bit nervous as unlike a match it’s out of his control. He’s hoping it goes his way, and has seen some friends and family. Told there’s not much more he could’ve done, he says there’s always more, and had he converted one of the Champions League and World Cup semis to silverware, he’d have taken it for sure. He backs himself as a finisher and as a creator, so with fast players around him and the way Bayern play, he’s able to drop deeper while still scoring the goals. He loves the way his teammates talk about him and hopes he wins tonight.

“I like to ask who would you pay the most to watch, rather than who is the best,” emails Fin, a bit of a follow-on from the email Josh sent regards Ronaldinho. Out of the current players my top three would be Yamal, Kvaratskhelia and Olise.”
They are probably our foremost artists, though I also love Pedri for that. As it goes, Dembélé was once in that category, then became a more serious accumulator.
Harry Kane arrives,hair McDonald’s arching as it does. In an amazing turn-up for the books, his suit isn’t a slick as Mbappé’s or even close to it – photo to follow.

“Joining a long line of people who say this popularity contest, leaked to you by Fabrizio, is dead to them after an injustice,” laments Jakob Mathiszig-Lee. “Nedved over Henry in 03 for me, but there’s plenty of others, Sneijder in 10 and Lewandowski in 20 and 21.”

I agree, those Messi/Ronaldo years were suboptimal. Essentially, Nedved got it for one performance, Juve v Real Madrid in the Champions League – though I actually think Ruud van Nistelrooy would’ve won the domestic awards were the voting done later in the season.

“How many of these candidates actually make you smile for the quality of their football and skills?” wonders Josh Goldblatt. “Maybe Lamine, but the last entertainer surely was Ronaldinho, 2005 winner.”
You set them up and I’ll stick them away: here’s a piece about the wonder of O Bruxo.
Otherwse, I think Olise is that type of player though not, of course that type of quality – perhaps yet – likewise Mbappé. I mean look at this from last week.

“Re ‘he’s the best finisher from 12-22 yards I’ve ever seen,’” begins Geoff Wignall. “I get that you’re too young to have seen Greaves, Eusebio, Best, Law or Cruyff – let alone Puskas, whom I also never saw - but are you really claiming he’s better from that range than Messi? ‘Cause he ain’t.”

I’m too young to have seen them in the flesh, but Denis Law was a penalty-box player, likewise Greaves. Best’s goalscoring is underappreciated – from 64-65 to 71-72, he scored 14, 17, 10, 32, 22, 23, 22, 27 – but he wasn’t as deadly from the edge of the box as Kane and I don’t think Messi was either. He is as good with curlers, but not the low-backlift laces.

Luis de la Fuente tells Dazn he’d like to manage in the Premier League eventually, which is an interesting one – the job is very different to the one he’s currently killing, and building a team to play in his style would not be at all easy.

“Your rationale for Kane not winning is just weird,” reckons Emmanuel Dairo. “Lamine had perhaps the worst World Cup of a certified superstar outside maybe post-elite Ronaldo in 2022. I don’t think it’s up for debate that Kane performed better in USA than him overall. As for playing for the best team argument, so did Yamal, and I’d go as far as saying Kane being a space-vacating cenre-forward was a big part of why someone like Michael Olise blossomed. Finally, for all Mbappe’s brilliance, his efforts ultimately led to nothing for club or country, unlike Kane.”
Olise was brilliant at Palace, which is why Bayern bought him and also brilliant for France – his performance against Senegal was better than any Kane delivered at the World Cup.

On Lamine, I think his work in La Liga is worth more than Kane’s in the Bundesliga, and he delivered in the World Cup semi, when, I’m afraid, Kane shrunk and, on Mbappe, I can’t be differentiating Kane from him by virtue of a title won with Bayern, given they’d managed 11 in a row before he arrived and Mbappe. brilliant at the World Cup, has the explosive ability that I want in my personal concepption of what a centre-forward should be.
“The Ballon d’Or is dead to me,” writes Marek Wojenski. “In the last decade or two it’s been a public relations contest but what finally did it was the cancellation of the award in 2020.
Lewandowski should have won it. Yes, as a Poland fan, I am bitter as we’re not likely to have another Polish candidate in my lifetime.”
I don’t know about that – we’ve had two in mine, the other being Zibi Boniek, and three since 1974, Kazimierz Deyna the missing man.

R9, we learn, will be presenting the men’s award. He won it in 1997, when there was no doubt whatsoever as to who the best player in the world was. To this day, I’ve seen no one so shockingly brilliant, a superhuman playing an entirely different sport to the rest. Here’s a piece on what made him so special.

I’m delighted to see Barbra Banda on the shortlist. Selfishly, I’d love her to come to the WSL – I think she’d be an incredible fit. Oh, and Putellas who has joined us in the UK, is in the house; she prepared an outfit but hasn’t prepared a speech. No matter, she owns some of the most articulate feet in the world.

I can’t for the life of me get on board with the line we’re now hearing: had Argentina somehow snaffled the World Cup, the award would have to be Messi’s. He’s still got plenty, of course, but a stuffy set-piece goal, say, or a 0-0 and penalty triumph wouldn’t have somehow made him the best in the world. It’s not a lifetime achievement award.

Talking of UK winners, it’s absolutely insane to think that, in 1968, three winners – Denis Law, Bobby Charlton and George Best – played in the same Manchester United team. Now, though, despite the money in the Premier League and with the exception of Erling Haaland and Bruno Fernandes, the best attackers are found in La Liga and Ligue 1. That looks likely to change only in the next generation and only if English clubs develop their own elite talent

DAZN have just interviewed Michael Owen, since the sad death of Kevin Keegan the only surviving British winner. If I’m honest, he did pretty well to get that, which isn’t to decry his efforts – in Rome and Cardiff especially – but the best player in the world? Not for me, Clive.
There appears to have been a leak: on the Ballon d’Or website, there’ve been articles lauding Kane, Mbappé and Lamine. That won’t surprise anyone, but of course the order is what really matters.

Lamine will, we have to assume, win the young player away for the third time on the spin. I think we can confidently say he was the best 16-year-old we’ve ever seen though, once he turned 17, Pelé had him beat.

Why, then, am I not going for Kane, seeing as you don’t ask. It’s a strange one given he’s the best finisher from 12-22 yards I’ve ever seen, and has reinvented his position, a prolific goalscorer but also a playmaker. However throughout his career, he’s not quite done it in the biggest games, and I just can’t anoint him the planet’s best for this season when he couldn’t get it done in the closing stages of either World Cup or Champions League – again. Killing the Bundesliga in by far its best team, even without him, and a brace against DR Congo, just isn’t enough, and ultimately, that’s why I’m going for Lamine – though, if you asked me who I think the best player in the world is, I’d probably say Mbappé, just.
So who should win? In the women’s competition, I’m going for the wondrous Alexia Putellas; I’m not sure many will argue to the contrary.

The men’s competition is a harder choice. I can’t decide between Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal, but I’m going for Lamine because he inspired Barcelona to the title and was easily the better of the two in the World Cup semi; in third, I’d go for Michael Olise, but I’m sure Harry Kane will be on the podium.
So who’s going to win? Well, first things first: the ceremony is being held in London to honour Stanley Matthews, who won the debut award 70 years ago.

One of the things we love about football is that, in a fickle world of questions, it offers us definitive answers. The best team in the league is the team which wins the league; in order to be certain who deserves to win a match, we’ve devised a handy metric to tell us, known as the score; and should we ever be unsure as to what silly haircut we should have next, what histrionic we should practise, or how best to flout authority, the beautiful game will surely supply us with an answer.

The Ballon d’Or, though, is a different state of affairs. Though the game offers us no parameters for judgment, it being a team sport, often it’s obvious which players have been the world’s best over a season. On other occasions, though, it’s a matter of criteria and opinion, which is where we find ourselves this evening.

But this term, we’ve no outstanding candidate on either men’s or women’s side, which allows us to enjoy plenty of conjecture and opinion, deconstructing this wonderful thing of ours to examine its constituent parts. Are we honouring the best or the most effective? Should we be looking for reliability or inspiration, impact or output, consistent excellence or big-game decisiveness? The next few hours will tell us what one journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the Fifa rankings think but, something else we love about football is that whenever decision is made and whatever it is, there’ll always be people desperate to tell those responsible why they’re wrong. Let’s do it!

articles.headline: Are We All Maxxed Out? Dictionary.com Names ‘Maxxing’ Its 2026 Word of the Year
keyFacts: Dictionary.com named 'maxxing' its Word of the Year for 2026, defining it as the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing life aspects.
Dictionary.com reported that popular variations in 2026 included looksmaxxing for physical appearance and tokenmaxxing for extensive AI use at work.
Dictionary.com stated that other words on its shortlist included affordability, data center, odyssey, and unc.
body: Are you focusmaxxing today? Knowledgemaxxing? Maybe fibermaxxing? Dictionary.com has chosen “maxxing,” which can seemingly be attached as a suffix to any other English word, as its Word of the Year for 2026.

Dictionary.com defines maxxing as “the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing a certain aspect of your life.” It’s not a lot different from older expressions such as taking it to the max, maxing out a credit card or feeling maxed out. Words like max, maximum and maximize have their roots in the Latin maximus — meaning “greatest” or “largest.”

But maxxing takes it to another level. The word has an additional x and can be tacked onto the back of seemingly any word. Dictionary.com said that two of the most common of these in 2026 have been looksmaxxing and tokenmaxxing.
More from CNET

Looksmaxxing — maximizing one’s physical appearance — was the most popular internet search term in 2026 for derivations of maxxing, according to Dictionary.com. Certain internet content creators popularized the term and have gained large followings with their sometimes extreme approaches to improving their looks.

Tokenmaxxing is another frequently searched term. In the world of AI, token refers to a small bit of written text that AI language models process to formulate responses. The term tokenmaxxing generally refers to using AI as much as possible at work, as companies integrate AI more and more into workflows. It’s no joke: Some companies are tracking and evaluating their workers on how much and how effectively they use AI in their jobs.
Maxxing can also be used on its own, such as, “Have you been maxxing on anything lately?”
Dictionary.com said the popularity of “maxxing” in all its various uses indicates how much we value optimization, as does the rising use of prefixes super- and ultra- in 2025.

“Whatever we’re doing, we want to push it further,” Dictionary.com reports. “But its expanding uses also reveal how people are responding to that impulse. Some embrace it. Some exaggerate it for laughs. Others flip it on its head to describe stepping away from the relentless pursuit of more. The open question is whether this need for optimization has peaked or if we’ll push even harder next year.”
If you let your imagination fly, you can maxx on anything — dietmaxxing to lose weight, bookmaxxing to read more, bingemaxxing for all that streaming.
Data center among the top 5

Dictionary.com’s shortlist of top words this year included affordability, data center (spelled as two words), odyssey and unc. Affordability has been one of the most common words in politics in the lead-up to the midterms — can people pay for what they need? Data centers are sprouting up all over the US and are either gateways to economic prosperity or harbingers of doom, depending on whom you talk to.

Unc, short for uncle, refers to someone who’s out of touch with Gen Z and Gen Alpha culture; and odyssey cracked the top five thanks to the popularity of The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s 2026 film adapted from Homer’s Greek epic about Odysseus’ journey home after the Trojan War.

articles.headline: UN sounds the alarm over Israel's West Bank military operation
keyFacts: UN officials criticized the Israeli military operation in Hebron that followed a deadly shootout.
The Hebron municipality stated that over 3,000 people were ordered to leave their homes during the operation.
The Israeli military stated that the operation would continue for several days.
body: The Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron was met with sharp criticism from the head of the UN as well as the UN's human rights commissioner in comments made on Monday.

The criticism comes after an Israeli military operation was launched in the occupied West Bank in response to a shootout on Friday that left two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen dead. Three more Israeli soldiers were also injured.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to demolish buildings in the West Bank city of Hebron and to close off the West Bank. It came just days before Israel's general election on Tuesday.
What did the UN say about Israeli operation in the West Bank?
The United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres said on Monday that "settlements are expanding, evictions are unrelenting with Palestinians driven from their lands," in a post on X.
"We are seeing an increasingly coercive environment, with the spectre of ethnic cleaning looming ever larger," he wrote.

The UN Human Rights High Commissioner Volker Türk also issued a statement condemning Israeli actions, saying the "aggressive operation" has resulted in the forcible displacement of thousands of Palestinians, "demolished homes and commercial property, and deprived residents of the ability to move freely."
"Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law. Threats to empty and erase entire neighbourhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing," he said.
A UN report, also released on Monday, that accuses Israel of committing war crimes in the West Bank, was rejected by the Israeli Foreign Ministry as "propaganda."

The ministry said that the findings were "not a human rights report but a propaganda document detached from reality, aimed at undermining Israel's right to self-defense, delegitimizing the Jewish state, and legitimizing jihadist terrorism against its citizens."
What is the Israeli operation in the West Bank?
Israeli troops entered the Deir Baha neighborhood, where the assailants lived, and ordered residents to pack up and leave.
The Hebron municipality said that more than 3,000 people, including 200 babies, were ordered to leave.

The Israeli military said at the weekend that its troops were carrying out precise, targeted and thorough searches to "locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure and locate weapons, alongside questioning suspects" in Hebron.
The military said the operation was expected to continue "for several days" and would focus on Deir Baha.
The largescale response to the firefight in the West Bank comes in the run-up to elections in Israel on Tuesday that could bring an end to Netanyahu's premiership.
Netanyahu has frequently painted himself as the only person who can keep Israel safe but his opponents have accused him of lacking a plan.

articles.headline: Vance puts American sovereignty at center of closing midterm argument
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance rallied Montana voters on Monday to support Republican congressional candidates by framing the midterm elections around American sovereignty.
Vance argued that Republican policies protect American jobs, border security, and public safety.
Vance, along with President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, campaigned in Montana to boost turnout for Republican candidates like Aaron Flint and Kurt Alme.
body: Vice President JD Vance rallied Montana voters to support Republican congressional candidates by framing the midterm elections as a choice between a post-racial sovereignty, supported by the GOP, and a system dominated by Democrats who don’t want the United States to thrive.

“In the last couple of years, we have cut down on visa fraud and fought against anybody who would lay off an American worker and replace them with a low-wage foreigner because sovereignty means that American jobs go to the American people,” Vance said Monday afternoon while speaking at an airplane hangar in Belgrade, Montana .

“Sovereignty means that you control your streets and that every American child, whether they are black or white, whether they are rich or poor, should be able to walk to a park or walk to a school without their parents worried about their safety,” Vance said. “And that is why Donald J. Trump closed the border on Day 1 and went to war against the drug cartels.”

Over the past two weeks, Vance, President Donald Trump, and House Speaker Mike Johnson have traveled to Montana to boost turnout for Aaron Flint, the Republican candidate for Montana’s 1st Congressional District, against Democrat Sam Forstag. The two men are vying to replace outgoing Rep. Ryan Zinke (R-MT).

Vance also campaigned for Republican Senate nominee Kurt Alme, who is running against independent Seth Bodnar, Democrat Alani Bankhead, and libertarian Kyle Austin. The contest is for an open seat after incumbent Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT) opted to retire this year.
Vance has framed the midterm elections as a battle for what kind of country the U.S. will be, invoking his childhood to sell the message.

“I remember as a kid driving around with my grandfather, a union welder at a steel mill who could identify the cars that were made with American steel, and he’d beam with pride when he did so,” Vance said about his childhood. “I remember playing pee wee football in leagues where the sons of working-class white kids played together on teams with the sons of working-class black kids, never worrying about the color of our skin or the relative privilege of black or white; we knew that we were privileged to grow up in the United States of America.”

Vance’s comments echoed, in some ways, former President Barack Obama’s 2004 racial unity speech at the Democratic National Convention, which put him on the national radar and sparked presidential rumors.

“There’s not a liberal America and a conservative America, there’s the United States of America,” Obama, then an Illinois state senator, said. “There’s not a black America and white America and Latino America and Asian America, there’s the United States of America.”
TRUMP’S $5,000 DIVIDEND PROMISE MET WITH SKEPTICISM AHEAD OF ELECTION DAY

Vance is widely considered a front-runner for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028 and has some similarities to Obama. The two men come from interracial families. Obama is the son of a white mother and a father from Kenya, while Vance, a white man, is married to Usha Vance, who’s of Indian descent, and has biracial children. Both are based in the Midwest.

Vance also served as a U.S. senator representing Ohio before becoming vice president, while Obama served as a U.S. senator from Illinois. Obama also similarly played coy about not running for president before ultimately launching his historic 2008 campaign.

articles.headline: Trump offers $1 million reward for tips resulting in voter fraud convictions
keyFacts: President Donald Trump announced a $1 million reward for tips reporting voter fraud that result in arrests and convictions.
The announcement occurred one week before polls close in the 2026 midterm elections during Trump's campaign travels.
Trump previously claimed that widespread voter fraud affected past elections and stated he ordered a lawsuit regarding Alaska's Senate race.
body: President Donald Trump said Monday that the administration will pay out $1 million to tipsters who report cases of voter fraud that result in convictions, just one week before the polls close in the 2026 midterm elections.

“Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Thank you for your attention to this matter.”

The statement was published as the president heads to Mississippi for a campaign rally to boost Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), who, polls show, runs in a close contest. It also comes as Trump is flexing the full extent of his political weight to boost Republicans heading into Election Day. The president has spent the better part of the past month crisscrossing the country, rallying for downballot candidates, where he consistently claims that Democrats have “rigged” past elections.

In Perry, Georgia, on Saturday, Trump repeated his claim that Sen. Jon Ossoff, who is running for reelection this cycle, would have lost his first Senate campaign in 2020 if it weren’t for widespread voter fraud in Georgia’s Fulton County. He has similarly suggested Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system, and the appearance on this year’s ballot of a candidate who bears the same first and surname of incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK), is an attempt by Democrats to steal the race.
Last week, the president said he ordered the Justice Department to file a lawsuit blocking the results of Alaska’s Senate race if Sullivan loses his reelection bid.
TRUMP: ‘PEOPLE DON’T TALK’ ABOUT DEMOCRATS’ STRONGEST 2028 CANDIDATE

Despite attempts from some Republicans to distance themselves from Trump’s past claims regarding voter fraud, the president maintains that his own 2020 election loss was the result of voter fraud perpetrated in several states. Earlier this year, he lobbied congressional Republicans to pass the SAVE America Act, which would restrict voting by mail and institute additional election security measures, though the legislation failed to pass the U.S. Senate.

articles.headline: Unhinged NC state Senate candidate arrested after live-posting through police standoff: ‘I have 6 rounds and the high ground’
keyFacts: North Carolina state Senate candidate Jonathan D. Miller was arrested Monday following an armed standoff with police in woods near Raleigh.
Miller live-posted updates on X during the incident, stating he fled into the woods after police approached him about suicidal threats.
Police took Miller into custody Monday afternoon without any shots being fired, according to local news reports.
body: An unhinged North Carolina state Senate candidate live-posted his own armed standoff with cops Monday, posting alarming updates from the woods as he claimed officers were closing in on him.
Jonathan D. Miller, the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina’s 16th Senate District in the suburbs of Raleigh, was taken into custody Monday afternoon with no shots fired, WRAL reported.
Miller began posting Sunday night that he intended to take his own life — then gave live updates when cops showed up to his apartment in Cary, outside Raleigh, Monday morning.
Miller refused an order to keep his hands away from a pistol at his hip and then ran into some nearby woods, he told WRAL.
“The whole police department is chasing me with guns drawn. This should be fun,” he wrote on X after fleeing.
Miller posted that he “has six shots and the high ground” as officers closed in, adding that he hoped police wouldn’t find him but that a confrontation would be “a hell of a show.”
“I f—-d up and talked to the negotiator on the phone long enough for them to box me in. They have dogs so I’m probably done for,” he later wrote.
Miller, who describes himself as a carpenter and former small-business owner, is running against a Democratic incumbent and a Republican contender in the Nov. 3 election.
He called a local news station during the standoff and explained his reasons for the suicidal threats.

“Last night I was pretty depressed and suicidal, and I sort of put a suicide note on X, and it has gone quite viral … I spent all night crying, and angry, and upset, and depressed, and all the emotions. And this morning I was tired, but I had things I needed to do. And I didn’t kill myself,” he told WRAL.

“So I got up and made coffee … and while I was having a cigarette, a police officer approached me, knew my name, saw that I had a holstered revolver on my hip, so he drew his weapon and told me to keep my hands away from mine. I told him I was going to refuse that order, and I backed away slowly until I was far enough away from him to turn and run, and then I turned and ran into the woods,” he continued.

If you are struggling with suicidal thoughts or are experiencing a mental health crisis and live in New York City, you can call 1-888-NYC-WELL for free and confidential crisis counseling. If you live outside the five boroughs, you can dial the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention hotline at 988 or go to SuicidePreventionLifeline.org.

body: Former South Carolina Republican and Democratic governors unite behind Democrat's bid for US Senate

The two former governors, who once faced off against each other, acknowledged that while they don’t agree on everything, they agree on Andrews as the best candidate to put South Carolina first.
“Annie understands that leadership isn’t about making people angrier. Well, it’s about making things better,” says Beasley. “She’s willing to put people ahead of politics,” adds Hodges.
Beasley adds:
We may have served as your governor from different political parties. But we agree South Carolina deserves better than more of the same political fighting.
Andrews, a paediatrician, is looking to flip the seat, currently held by Darline Graham, sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham.
Trump makes baseless claim Lula's victory in Brazil 'looked like another rigged election'

Speaking to reporters as he left for a campaign rally in Mississippi on Monday, Donald Trump said that the comeback victory of Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, over his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, “looked like another rigged election, frankly.”

“It was a terrible look, for the world,” Trump said, apparently referring to the court-ordered extension in voting hours after widespread reports that supporters of the president had been hindered in getting to the polls by public transportation outages.
“You know, elections have to be indisputable — and it looked very bad to me,” the US president added. “It looked so corrupt.”

None of the reporters in the limited press pool, after reporters from CNN and Politico were again blocked from taking part, pointed out to Trump that Brazil’s supreme court only extended voting hours across the nation by two hours after requests from both candidates.

The correspondent who was questioning Trump was Cara Castronuova a former reality TV fitness trainer now covering the White House for LindellTV, the streaming platform created by Mike Lindell, the election conspiracy theorist pillow salesman.

As our colleagues in Brazil reported earlier, the president of Brazil’s electoral court, justice Kassio Nunes Marques, who was appointed by the Bolsonaro’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, said that extending voting hours had caused “no change” to the election result.

Asked if he intended to intervene in any way, Trump said: “Well, I’m not running Brazil. I’m running the USA. And I just thought that the election was – I like Lula. I get along with him very well. I just think it had a very bad look, the election, the way it was tabulated. The extension given was very strange.”
Trump promises $1m reward for voter fraud tips the result in conviction
In a post to his personal social media platform on Monday afternoon, President Trump promised to pay $1m to anybody who submits a report of voter fraud resulting in an arrest and conviction.
“Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!” Trump wrote.

Trump has alleged for years, without evidence, that widespread voter fraud by noncitizens has tipped the scales in US elections, including in his 2020 re-election defeat. He’s made the issue a centerpiece of his domestic agenda in his second term, aggressively pushing legislation and executive orders that he says would root out illegal votes, but that critics (and the courts, in some cases) have argued would disenfranchise eligible voters and overstep federal authority.
While Trump is heading down south to stump for Republicans in Mississippi, JD Vance, his vice-president and one of his top surrogates on the midterm campaign trail, is heading west.

After a campaign stop in Montana earlier today, Vance will head to straight to Kansas, advocating for Republicans in both deep-red states as Republicans look to shore up their margins in races typically seen as safe.

In Belgrade, Montana, Vance was campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Kurt Alme, among others. He also laughed off comments Trump made in recent days commenting on the figures (butts, in particular) of both Jon Husted, the Republican Senate candidate in Ohio, and rapper Nikki Minaj.
“We’re self-confident men in the Trump-Vance administration,” Vance quipped. “The President’s been noticing a lot about the physiques of everyone lately.”
Israeli voters go to the polls in election overshadowed by war with Iran

Tomorrow, Israel will hold its first election since the surprise attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023 – an incursion that killed 1,200 people and kickstarted an ever-escalating regional conflict in the Middle East.

Since then, Israel has launched a series of wars against Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, while settlers have escalated state-backed efforts to displace Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Under the leadership of Benjamin Netanyahu, the longtime prime minister, Israel has also found itself increasingly isolated on the world stage due to the scale of its civilian killings in Gaza and elsewhere, even as the Trump administration has stood by it.

Domestically, the coalition formed by Netanyahu has taken aim at democratic institutions, including the supreme court. Many Israelis have described this election as the most consequential in their country’s history.
It’s also consequential for Donald Trump, who launched the war with Iran alongside Netanyahu and has backed him for reelection.
My colleague Emma Graham-Harrison breaks down the Israeli election, and what’s at stake, here.
Lawsuit from news consumers targets Trump's restrictions on White House press

A new lawsuit filed in federal court on Monday against the Trump administration sought to end the president’s practice of banning or restricting White House access to news outlets whose coverage he finds unfavorable.

But instead of from one of the spurned media outlets, the suit originated with a different kind of plaintiffs: news consumers, who claim that Trump’s actions deprive them of their rights to “receive news coverage that is not limited by the president’s unlawful expulsions or distorted by the president’s unconstitutional threats”.

The five plaintiffs – who describe themselves in the complaint as a human rights advocate, a media watchdog, a historian, a civics teacher, a legal journalist and a student journalist – alleged that the harms to news consumers go beyond the loss of reporting from directly banned outlets. They said it also extends to other outlets that are pressured to soften their reporting, lest they face a similar ban.

“Some of the news organizations targeted by the Policy have sued, arguing, correctly, that the First Amendment requires that their access be restored,” the plaintiffs wrote. The ultimate injury here, however, is to the democratic public.”

They continued: “Defendants’ Policy of restricting the access of disfavored news organizations deprives the public of the reporting of those organizations, and it inevitably deprives them of the independent reporting of other news organizations as well, since every journalist who reports from the White House must now account for the possibility that a critical or ill-advised word about the president may result in their access being summarily restricted or revoked.”

In his most recent and most sweeping attack on the White House press since the start of his second term, Trump banned three outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – from the White House, accusing them of peddling “fake news”. After a brief standoff with the wider White House press corp, a judge stepped in to restore the three outlets’ access while the case winds its way through the courts.
Judge rules Maurene Comey's firing from the Department of Justice was illegal

A federal judge found on Monday that the Trump administration has overstepped in firing Maurene Comey, the daughter of the former FBI director and Trump opponent James Comey, the Associated Press reported.

Comey, who was fired from her job as a federal prosecutor last year, alleged in a lawsuit against the justice department that the move was unconstitutional retaliation against her for her relationship to her father and her perceived political alignment.
Judge Jesse Furman, ruling on Monday, sided with the younger Comey, ordering that she be reinstated in her role and given back pay.

Trump heads to unexpected battleground Mississippi as Democrats try for shock Senate flip

Donald Trump is heading to Corinth, Mississippi today for a rally at 7pm ET, as he continues a closing midterm campaign blitz that has seen him dispatch to even some of the nation’s most reliably red states, which have turned into unexpected battlegrounds.

The Magnolia state, which hasn’t elected a Democratic senator since 1982, is probably not where the GOP envisioned needing a late-October stop from the president. But Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith is facing a stiff challenge from Scott Colom, one of many Democratic underdogs that have managed to expand the House and Senate battleground maps amid widespread voter discontent over inflation, the war against Iran and other aspects of Trump’s second presidency.

Hyde-Smith, who is vying for her second full term, remains the favorite in a state that Trump won three times by an average of nearly 20 percentage points. But Colom, a local prosecutor who would make history Mississippi’s first Black senator since the post-civil war Reconstruction era, is looking to parlay inflation, Trump’s lagging popularity and Hyde-Smith’s mistakes into an upset.

Colom has outpaced Hyde-Smith in fundraising since he launched his campaign last year, and he caught national attention this month with a viral ad that mocked Hyde-Smith, a former state agriculture commissioner, dismissing risingbeef prices, driven higher by Trump’s tariffs and fuel spikes resulting from the war on Iran. The ad features Hyde-Smith saying that consumers “have so many other proteins to choose from” - followed by several characters declaring: “Pick another protein? I’d rather pick another senator.”

Colom’s campaign followed with a social media video that featured an AI-generated Hyde-Smith dodging questions about that controversy and other issues. The Democrat took down the video after the Mississippi attorney general said it could violate state law barring the use of deepfakes so close to election day.

Senate Democrats’ Super Pac, meanwhile, has been a late entry in the contest, with a $1.2m investment – a paltry sum compared to Senate contests in more populous states like Texas or Georgia but an amount that can go farther in Mississippi’s smaller television markets.
Trump calls Bill Maher a ‘total loser’ in 1,300-word Truth Social rant
Donald Trump launched a 1,300-word social media rant against late-night US TV host Bill Maher yesterday evening, calling him a “TOTAL LOSER” in a fresh assault on the media.

“Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher,” the US president wrote. “He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement – But that’s all gone.”
Trump’s lengthy and detailed post about Maher came after the host interviewed Karoline Leavitt, the former White House press secretary, on his program Real Time with Bill Maher.
Maher asked Leavitt about Trump’s “lame duck” presidency and whether the president would act on “vengeance” if Republicans largely lose to Democrats in next week’s midterms.

“I worry that if this election goes as badly as it looks like it’s going to go for him and the Republicans, we’re going to have a guy who doesn’t have as much power as he did … and we know he likes vengeance,” Maher told Leavitt.
Leavitt remained steadfast in her support for Trump and expressed confidence that Republicans could still outperform expectations.
Trump called Maher a “coward who is afraid to tell the truth about how well our Country is running”, claiming that Maher praised him behind the scenes but on television insults him with jokes.

“Also, turn your Laugh Machine off, it’s a joke when they laugh uncontrollably, even when you say nothing funny, and I’m going to have the Republicans not cover you anymore, because they try to talk about you as a guy who is transformative,” Trump wrote.
But Trump’s lengthy attack on Maher is notable, coming just about a week until the US midterm elections, where Republicans are trying to fend off challenges from Democratic opponents.
Catholic bishops say they regret joining Trump in Oval Office prayer
Joseph Gedeon

Two Catholic bishops who bowed their heads with Donald Trump in the Oval Office now say they regret it, accusing the White House of turning a private prayer into a campaign photo opportunity before next week’s US elections.

Archbishop Jeffrey Grob of Milwaukee and Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines, who were among the 12 bishops who met administration officials last Thursday, issued separate statements of regret over the weekend.

The fallout stems from the White House quickly posting video and photos of the prayer on social media, captioned as Catholic archbishops and bishops praying with the US president, less than two weeks before the midterm elections on 3 November.

Archbishop Grob issued a statement headlined A Public Apology, in which he said he felt “a heavy sadness” over the pain the images had caused, and that he had heard from people alarmed that he had unwittingly joined a political event on the eve of a national vote.

Others, he said, were hurt because of the effect of Trump’s policies on their families. “We should never have been put in that position by the White House,” wrote Grob, adding that he had harbored reservations and “wish I had heeded them”.
Bishop Joensen wrote that “many things tied to this present Administration” were “blatantly at odds with our Catholic faith”.

He said none of the bishops was unaware the meeting fell close to an election, but insisted that none had intended to endorse a party or candidate. “I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purposes.”

Grob said the Heritage Foundation, the conservative thinktank behind the Project 2025 rightwing blueprint for the second Trump administration, arranged the meeting. The bishops, he said, were told it would be a private discussion of immigration enforcement, religious-worker visas and human dignity, with a possible chance to pray privately with the president.

After 90 minutes with domestic policy staff, they were ushered into the Oval Office, handed commemorative tokens and, Grob detailed, directed to stand behind Trump’s desk and pray. Nobody told them a video was being recorded, he said, and they never agreed to its release.
“I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro”: Abdul El-Sayed to Trump at campaign event
Abdul El-Sayed responded on Monday after Donald Trump’s Islamophobia-laced rant against the Michigan Democratic Senate candidate during a campaign event in the state over the weekend.
During that speech, Trump referred to Abdul El-Sayed as “Muhammad”, playing up a Muslim stereotype, and accused him of being a jihadist with designs of instating sharia law in the US.
“I don’t even care that he remembers my whole name,” El-Sayed shot back on Monday, addressing a campaign crowd in Grand Rapids. “Because he can just go on and call me ‘senator’ after November.”
He added: “I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro.”
Earlier, El-Sayed also accused the president of attacking him for his faith while engaging in self-dealing with allies in the Islamic world.

“I get that the president of the United States takes personal offense to my first name,” El-Sayed said. “He doesn’t mind as much when it’s a shared name from the Saudis who are funding his son-in-law’s private equity, doesn’t seem to mind as much when it’s the Qataris who are giving him a $400m private jet.”

articles.headline: Winston’s copypasta fever might be my favorite celebration of Overwatch
keyFacts: Overwatch fans have been sharing a social media copypasta about Winston, the game's gorilla character from the moon.
Destructoid reported that the trend provides silly joy to both avid and lapsed players of the game.
The copypasta features a description of Winston's traits, including his Tesla cannon and dome shield.
body: I’m being jumped by Winston everywhere I look, and I don’t even have Overwatch installed. Fans have been flooding social media with a new copypasta involving the game’s super smart gorilla from the moon, and I can’t help but enjoy it.

The premise is devilishly simple . It starts off by leading the conversation in one direction, but it closes in on a nod to Winston, usually with some variation of “smart gorilla from the moon with a Tesla cannon and a dome shield to counter AoE slop.”

Deadlock’s biggest strength is its character design, but so far none of its cast is truly original. Rat King, really? A rat in New York? What about a gorilla? He could be super smart and from the moon, with a short range toggle Tesla cannon, and a dome shield to counter aoe slop. https://t.co/VsA1HYjG4f
— tats (@ltats__) October 23, 2026

I haven’t really been invested in Overwatch since before the fiasco that was Overwatch 2 . The promised and undelivered PvE mode was bad enough, and the shift to an absurd monetization model made me happily stop dedicating any time to the game. And that’s without diving into the company’s chilling cornucopia of controversies.

Yet the game seems to be back on track, thankfully dropping the “2” from its name and delivering quite a lot on the gameplay front. It feels a lot better to play now that it has content rather than just being a way to print money with Kiriko skins, as it seemed to be early in OW2 (and no, the shift to five-vs-five and three new heroes weren’t nearly enough to warrant the rebrand).
Image via Blizzard Entertainment Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !

As someone who played a lot of Overwatch before dropping it for good, there’s something comforting about seeing it touch the lives of so many people that, 10 years since its release, it still has a place to bring silly joy to avid and lapsed players alike. This seemed to be organic, too—a nice change of pace from when the community has to band together to ask for more than crumbs .

A part of me misses the halcyon days of my 20s, before the pandemic, when I’d check if my friends were up for some games before I’d even gotten home from work. I miss tuning into the Overwatch League matches, the build-up to new hero releases, and even the lore crumbs. We finally got Junker Queen, D.Mon, and Jetpack Cat, which have been teased in some form for years. That alone would have made 2018 me freak out (though Mama Hong is still nowhere to be seen).

I’ve stopped playing Overwatch , but I still watch friends grind ranked a couple of times a week on Discord. I once heard an enemy Genji ulting on stream and pressed Q to use Transcendence out of reflex, which would have been impressive if I weren’t in the middle of a different game entirely (old habits die hard).

I like to think there’s some maturity in recognizing you’ve outgrown something yet still carry fondness for it, be it a game, a decision, or even a relationship. Certain memories don’t always fully leave us, and that’s fine.

Likewise, I see bravery in not rushing toward a situation just because it’s familiar, especially if it’s not right for you. Sometimes old ghosts chase us, and they might just catch up if we’re not careful.
But you know what would make those ghosts scarier? If they were super smart gorillas from the moon, with short-range Tesla cannons and a dome shield to counter AoE slop.

articles.headline: The best haunted card game since Inscryption is back with a new mystery only solitaire freaks can solve
keyFacts: Forbidden Solitaire has released a new DLC called The Discarded, adding 30 new levels and challenging new gameplay mechanics.
Players control a character named Robyn Cierra who is searching for their sister while uncovering a mystery surrounding the 1995 CD-ROM game.
The DLC is currently priced at $8, while the base game is discounted to $11.51 for the next week.
body: The first new card I found in Forbidden Solitaire's new DLC The Discarded gave me the power to throw a card like a knife at whatever horror was trying to kill me. Although nothing warranted such a desperate move, I fear it won't be long before I find myself out of options now that I've seen the devilish new tricks the developers have dealt in the DLC's first hour.

I'm lucky I just spent the last week playing through the base game because The Discarded offers no help: From the moment you double click the DLC executable on the game's '90s-inspired PC interface, you're on your own. It's not quite enough to understand how to play solitaire; you need to know how to play Forbidden Solitaire, a haunted version of the classic card game where you must change your approach based on the modified cards the developers throw at you.

Some cards might be locked away until you play the right suits. Others might be surrounded by bones, requiring them to be played twice before leaving the board. Your deck will run out quickly if you don't strategize around these factors and try to knock off as many cards as you can in one turn.

Thankfully, you can cheat… by jamming gems into your flesh. The eyeball in the wall that compels you to mutilate your hand for power is back. This time, you can even sear glyphs into your skin, too. Each unholy decoration gives you bonuses that can help tilt the balance in your favor, like an increased chance to deal extra damage during combat—oh yeah, there's combat.

Right away, The Discarded's enemies don't play around. In the original game, you're taught to pay close attention to whatever horrible thing a monster plans to do once you finish your turn. This can be simply an attack that drains your health or a variety of curses that warp the cards. The beast at the start of the DLC can block you from playing cards by covering them in wet paint, and later you have to deal with marbled cards that don't contribute to your combos—and thus your damage.

I never knew solitaire could have so much depth until I played Forbidden Solitaire, and The Discarded sprinkles even more challenges that change your approach to what is otherwise a pretty straightforward game.

It also helps that there's an entire mystery to unravel as you go. You play the new DLC as Robyn Cierra, a character digging through Forbidden Solitaire, the in-universe 1995 CD-ROM game, in search of their sister. There's another character sending you texts with images and fuzzy FMV clips that detail all the bizarre events surrounding the development of the game, back in the early '90s. And if it's like the base game's story, I don't expect things to stay relatively normal for long.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Forbidden Solitaire is easily one of the best indie card games I've played since Inscryption and The Discarded DLC feels like a spooky encore. If you missed it, I recommend spending the two to three hours it takes to finish the base game first. That way you're prepared for whatever horrors await in the DLC's 30 new levels.
Forbidden Solitaire is currently $11.51, a few bucks off of its normal $16 price for the next week, and you can grab The Discarded DLC for $8.

While his specialty is in action RPGs and MMOs, he's driven to cover all sorts of games whether they're broken, beautiful, or bizarre.
