articles.headline: NFL trade rumors: 4 potential landing spots for Maxx Crosby if Raiders decide to sell at deadline
keyFacts: The Las Vegas Raiders dropped to a 3-4 record, sparking speculation about whether the organization will trade star pass rusher Maxx Crosby before the November 10 deadline.
CBS Sports senior NFL writer Pete Prisco argued that the Raiders should trade Crosby to acquire draft capital for their ongoing rebuild.
Potential landing spots for Crosby include the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, and Buffalo Bills.
body: The Las Vegas Raiders have now gone from 3-0 to 3-4. Just a few weeks ago, they were one of the biggest surprises in the NFL, but have since become a losing team that could be making a quarterback change in the near future. Their swift fall from undefeated to losing record could also change how the organization approaches the upcoming trade deadline.

It's again time to debate if the Raiders should trade one of their best players, pass rusher Maxx Crosby. We listed him as a player but it remains to be seen if that's in the cards for Vegas. Crosby was traded to the Baltimore Ravens this offseason for two first-round picks. However, the Ravens backed out of the deal when their staff discovered something worrisome during the in-person physical.

ESPN's Adam Schefter mentioned recently that it's unknown if Crosby is pushing for a trade behind closed doors, as he was several months ago. Maybe he viewed the canceled trade with Baltimore as divine intervention signaling he was meant to be a Raider for life. Plus, what would Vegas want for him at this point? It's hard to imagine the Raiders fetching two first-round picks again.

With that said, senior NFL writer Pete Prisco argued on CBS Sports HQ this past Sunday that the Raiders should trade Crosby and pick up further draft capital to help in the rebuild they are currently in. Those picks, he said, could be used when Fernando Mendoza eventually takes over.
Should the Raiders try to trade Maxx Crosby before the NFL Trade Deadline? 🤔@PriscoCBS says it should be heavily considered. #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/azjOOezxuD
— NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 26, 2026

Maybe Crosby only fetches a first-round pick and a fourth-round pick this time around. Is that good enough for Raiders' GM John Spytek to consider? Crosby is one of the best defensive ends in the NFL. Not only does he get after quarterbacks, having recorded four double-digit sack seasons, but no player has recorded more tackles for loss (136) since Crosby entered the league in 2019. His 25 pressures this season rank second in the NFL behind Greg Rousseau.

The Raiders trading Crosby prior to the Nov. 10 deadline would be a bit surprising. If they decided to part ways with a star talent, where could Crosby land? Let's take a look at four potential landing spots.
Chicago Bears

The Chicago Bears were deemed the prime regression candidate in the NFC this year following their magical 11-6 campaign in 2025, when they registered an NFL-record seven wins when trailing in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, including playoffs. But with Caleb Williams under center, who says Chicago has to regress? The Bears do have some tough games coming up against the Seattle Seahawks, Detroit Lions, Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills, but through seven weeks, Chicago is sitting pretty at 5-2.

The Bears' pass rush could be improved. It's pretty unbelievable that cornerback Kyler Gordon has played in just two games this season and is tied with Austin Booker for the team lead with four sacks. Chicago also just saw Montez Sweat get suspended two games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing drugs policy, while Dayo Odeyingbo is currently out with a quadriceps injury. The Bears make sense for Crosby if he's moved.
Detroit Lions

There's another team in the NFC North where Crosby could potentially be a fit, and it's the team he grew up rooting for. The Lions are actually tied for the league lead in sacks this season with 21, but the defense still ranks dead last with 391.0 yards allowed per game.

I think it's possible Kelvin Sheppard's unit is on the upswing. Not only did they hold Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers to 17 points on Sunday, but Brian Branch is back in the lineup, and Kerby Joseph could be back soon as well. Imagine if the Lions added Crosby to rush the passer opposite of Aidan Hutchinson? Maybe this is more wishful thinking, but the Lions could become the new favorite in the NFC North if they made this deal.
Dallas Cowboys

Some people, like myself, thought the Dallas Cowboys defense was going to be much improved in 2026. That has not been the case, as they rank third-worst in total yards allowed per game (382.5) entering their Monday night matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Cowboys took a swing on former Pittsburgh Steelers corner Joey Porter Jr., and they could make another deal in acquiring a pass rusher to help boost a unit that is tied for fourth-worst in sacks with eight. This would be an aggressive and controversial swing of the bat from Jerry Jones.
Buffalo Bills

Let's get a little wild. The Bills made it clear they were "Super Bowl or bust" when they fired Sean McDermott last year, but this Jim Leonhard defense needs some work. Buffalo has won four games this year, and all four victories came in matchups where the Bills allowed 30+ points! The rest of the NFL was 8-42 through Week 6 in games where defenses allowed at least 30 points. The Bills ranked first in points per drive (3.13) and last in points per drive allowed (2.76) after Week 6.
Imagine pairing Greg Rousseau and Deone Walker with a talent like Crosby, and what that could do for this defense and team at large.

articles.headline: Dem bucks party over alleged Alaska vote-siphoning effort: 'Neither party should be doing it'
keyFacts: Iowa Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand criticized an alleged Democratic effort to siphon votes from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
Republicans and the Justice Department argued that the similar name of unaffiliated candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. could confuse voters.
Democratic opponent Mary Peltola and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer condemned the Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the race.
body: Iowa Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand is criticizing an alleged effort by Democrats to "siphon" votes from a Republican senator, calling the tactic "manipulating the political system" as the controversy consumes Alaska's bruising Senate race.

Sand was asked by Fox News about allegations that Democrats have boosted unaffiliated Alaska Senate candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., whose name closely resembles that of incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, in an effort to draw votes away from the senator.
"Both parties are doing it and neither party should be doing it," Sand told Fox News in an exclusive interview Sunday. "To me, it's manipulating the political system and it's not a good thing to do."
TOP ELECTION SCHEMES ROILING KEY MIDTERM RACES AS BOTH PARTIES ACCUSE RIVALS OF TRICKERY

The unusual candidacy has become the center of an escalating legal and political fight in Alaska, where the Justice Department has intervened, arguing that the similarity between the candidates' names could confuse voters. On the ballot, the Republican incumbent appears as "Dan S. Sullivan," identified as a Republican and the incumbent, while his unaffiliated challenger appears as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr."

Republicans argue the similarity could cause some voters intending to support the senator to instead select his unaffiliated challenger, accusing Democratic operatives of helping elevate Daniel J. Sullivan to "siphon" votes from the GOP incumbent. Democrats have blasted the Trump administration's intervention, while Daniel J. Sullivan has denied that he is a Democratic plant.
TRUMP SAYS 'WE ARE LOOKING INTO' OTHER DAN SULLIVAN ON ALASKA BALLOT, WARNS ABOUT GOVERNOR'S RACE

Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to his Democratic opponent, Mary Peltola.

The administration says the lawsuit is intended to address the possible voter confusion, but Peltola called the case "flagrant corruption," while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has called it "an outrage."
MANCHIN CALLS SCHUMER 'CRAZY' FOR TRYING TO OUST GOP SENATOR IN CRUCIAL SENATE SHOWDOWN
"This is an outrage," Schumer said on social media about the suit. "It shows they know they’re going to lose. We will fight tooth and nail. And we will win."
Peltola has argued that voters can distinguish between the two candidates and her campaign has asked a federal judge to dismiss the Justice Department's case.

articles.headline: Martin Keown and Alex Crook in heated clash live on air over Man United crisis
keyFacts: TalkSPORT journalists Alex Crook and Martin Keown had a heated live on-air debate on Monday regarding Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United manager.
The clash occurred after Manchester United's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left the team winless in eight matches.
TalkSPORT understands dressing room insiders expect club officials to sack Carrick following the poor run of results.
body: Manchester United’s ongoing crisis prompted a fiery exchange live on talkSPORT on Monday morning.
The Red Devils’ problems deepened on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.
Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook clashed with Martin Keown live on air amid United’s ongoing crisis talkSPORT
United are now winless in eight matches and talkSPORT understands dressing room insiders expect Michael Carrick to be sacked as manager.
Amid the issues facing the club, talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook joined Sam Matterface , Martin Keown and Dean Ashton on air.
Crook and Keown clash amid United crisis
Having provided an update on Carrick’s future, though, he quickly became embroiled in a heated back-and-forth with Keown.
The exchange stemmed from the former Arsenal defender asking Crook about his status as a United supporter.
Keown said: “Alex, not to blow your cover, but you’re a Manchester United fan, aren’t you?”
“Why are you not in the camp of the fans applauding Carrick off the pitch?”
Carrick was applauded off the pitch at Old Trafford by the home crowd, who had booed the United players at half-time and full-time on Sunday.
Crook replied: “I am. How do you know I’m not?” before Keown added: “Well, you just want change. You want him out.”
In response, Crook said: “I didn’t say that,” only for the former England international to continue: “You implied that.”

As their back-and-forth raged on, Crook reiterated: “I said my information as a journalist is there’s going to be a change, whether I think that’s the right or wrong decision, I think it’s inevitable.”
Keown questioned Crook’s stance on Carrick’s United future talkSPORT
When asked what he thinks United should do next, he explained: “I don’t think Michael Carrick is the biggest issue at Manchester United.
“I don’t think the manager has ever been the biggest issue at Manchester United.

“I think the Stretford End conducted themselves with great dignity yesterday, making their feelings towards a club legend, someone who clearly has put his all into this job, very clear and also voicing their disdain for a group of players who week in, week out, let them down, not just the fans, but the manager himself as well.
“He won’t say it, Michael Carrick, because he’s too much of a diplomat. He still cares too much about the football club. He will feel hurt by the performance of this season.

“How can you go from beating everybody around you last season to qualify for the Champions League to turning in the tripe that they are this season, that lack of effort, that lack of endeavor, that lack of accountability?”
Keown was not finished, though, as he responded: “So you’re separating the manager.
Crook accused Keown of ‘putting words’ in his mouth during their exchange talkSPORT
“You’re looking at the iconic player and not looking at the manager that you see before you now.”
Crook then hit back, saying: “Why are you putting words into my mouth, Martin? I’m not going to say that.”
The exchange then concluded with Keown adding: “But you are. That’s what it seems like.
“If we’re in the dressing room, taking you into the dressing room, it’s not an us and them situation.
“If we win, we all get the credit. If we lose, then it’s all of our fault. Everybody.”
Latest on Carrick’s future
As of Monday evening, Carrick has not been sacked by the Red Devils .
Carrick is expected to be sacked by United Getty
However, club officials expect the former United midfielder to be relieved of his duties just five months after signing a two-year deal.
His squad had a day off on Monday following their heavy defeat to the Cherries, with no training session held at Carrington.
Boardroom talks were expected to take place in the morning, with a decision not yet communicated to the manager regarding his future.
Carrick was present at the training ground, though, attending an Under-21s fixture against Hull City .
He was joined by assistant manager Steve Holland and Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher .

articles.headline: Mass Effect fans ramp up efforts to save BioWare's RPG series with a Times Square billboard and plans for more ads outside The Game Awards
keyFacts: Fans launched the Save Mass Effect movement after publisher EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next game in the series.
Organizers and content creator Kala Elizabeth placed a billboard in Times Square and plan further ads near EA offices and at The Game Awards.
Organizer Mer Mora stated that community crowdfunding will pay for the ads, with excess donations going to the Game Workers' Hardship Fund.
body: Fans continue to rally around the 'Save Mass Effect' movement, this time with a billboard at Times Square and more initiatives planned throughout the rest of the year.

Last week, publisher EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next Mass Effect game. In the days since, an increasingly loud community-organised campaign has attempted to make Electronic Arts reverse course and ensure that the beloved sci-fi universe can journey forward in some form.

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8
— We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) October 26, 2026

The We Are Mass Effect community group and content creator Kala Elizabeth are now collaborating on a number of initiatives, including a billboard at New York City's Times Square that points people toward the growing online "SaveMassEffect" hashtag. Text that reads "Kellah Si'yah" is sprawled across the ad - referencing the in-game ship that ferried different races to settle the Andromeda system.

"Apart from the Times Square billboard, we also have several other initiatives in the works. An advertising truck near EA's headquarters in Redwood City and in Edmonton, a mobile billboard for N7 Day, and another one in LA for The Game Awards. All of them will carry a message in support of #SaveMassEffect," one of the group's organisers, Mer Mora, told me via email.

The 'SaveMassEffect' petition gained a huge amount of traction this weekend with 226,000 signatures and counting. The petition urges rights holder EA to commit to "the continued development of Mass Effect" by either funding a new game in the series or by licensing it to an outside studio who can do it justice.

"All of these initiatives will be funded by the community itself! We're putting together a GoFundMe after receiving an overwhelming response from community members eager to contribute financially to make all of these happen," Mora added. "And given the incredible support and generosity we've received, any funds raised beyond our goal will be donated to the Game Workers' Hardship Fund, which supports game developers who have been laid off." The United Videogame Workers union (UVW-CWA) opened the fund earlier this year to support the many laid off video game workers across Canada and the USA.

articles.headline: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know
keyFacts: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic released regulatory paperwork detailing financial data, operational risks, and control structures ahead of its US stock market debut.
Anthropic disclosed that advanced AI could pose catastrophic risks to humanity, reporting a loss of $80.7bn in the first half of this year alongside $16.2bn in revenue.
The company stated it holds $131.6bn in working cash and relies heavily on a small fraction of its enterprise customers to support its business growth.
body: - Published
Artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic just released the required paperwork ahead of its long-anticipated debut on the US stock market.
The 335-page document included fresh details of how the Claude chatbot owner makes money, what it spends that money on and who it is controlled by.
Anthropic also detailed some of the the risks it claimed AI technology poses, including how it could take human lives. That information sat alongside the many purported benefits of the technology.
Here are five key points worth highlighting from the filing.
1. Armageddon is an occupational hazard
Every public company has to tell potential investors how things could go wrong.
Anthropic's "risk factors" were unique, also disclosing how the AI technology it is developing could doom humanity as a whole.

"Sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Anthropic said.

It noted that less than a year ago, a hacking group Anthropic believed to be sponsored by China "manipulated" Claude to successfully intrude on a number of institutions, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies and government agencies.
But Anthropic said its success is dependent on its ability to constantly "develop, improve, and deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models".

One of the most significant risks to that ability is Anthropic's access to infrastructure it needs, including computer chips and data centres, to build, train and operate the models that underpin its technology.
2. The company is haemorrhaging cash
Anthropic has yet to disclose a target share price for its stock listing.

The company is widely expected to debut with a market valuation of $2 trillion or more, making it the largest stock listing in history. But the figure will be heavily influenced by its financial performance.
Anthropic lost $80.7bn (Â£60bn) in the first half of this year, double what it lost across 2025 altogether.
The company's overall revenue was $16.2bn billion for the six-month period. Revenues are rising rapidly, but the firm has a long way to go before it breaks even.

Troy Hooper, co-head of equity capital markets at Mergermarket, said Anthropic's revenue growth is "exceptional". But investors are "less forgiving" of tech companies promising huge future returns than they were even months ago, he added.
Anthropic's debt picture is also unclear given it has a huge amount of accounting charges related to certain forms of investment.
"As a result, investors do not yet have a clear view of Anthropic's underlying profitability or whether its rate of cash generation is sufficient to support the business as it scales," Hooper added.
3. But luckily it has plenty of cash on hand
Despite losing money, Anthropic has heaps of cash lying about.
At $131.6bn, almost all of its cash in hand is defined as "working capital", meaning it can use the money to fund its operations day-to-day.
Currently, Anthropic has more cash on hand than Meta and Google combined.
Anthropic's costs could rise as it faces fierce competition for top staff and computing power from other AI giants.
The leasing of data centres alone is costing the company $321.4bn so far this year.
Hooper said such large costs are expected to grow. Even with this kind of cash, it won't be enough to maintain its business growth.
Any investors in Anthropic "will be paying for future dominance, not present-day economics", he said.
4. Anthropic relies on a few big customers
Anthropic sees boundless ways it can sell its technology to customers.
A large portion of its current business comes from just 250 major enterprise customers, which it says have paid it at least $10mn in the past year.
An even smaller number, just five enterprise customers, make up a quarter of its current business.
Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founder ETF, pointed out that "many top Anthropic customers have no long-term contract".
The company's level of business concentration leaves Anthropic dependent on a small fraction of its paying customers to support its growth, with no guarantee it will continue.

Anthropic also has enterprise relationships with the likes of Google and Amazon, both of which are also investors in the company "and competitors", creating potential business conflicts in the future, Monaghan noted.
Anthropic said its overall enterprise customer base has grown rapidly, going from roughly 1,500 customers last year to almost 12,000 this year.
Part of its growth strategy is offering Claude tools for free before working to "convert these users into paying customers over time".
The strategy has led to Claude seeing "the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history", the company claimed.
5. AI promises 'extraordinary' benefits to the world
For all of the risks Anthropic has said AI poses, it also reiterated its claim AI will produce an "extraordinary" amount of good.
"Achieving our mission means the world gains the enormous benefits of frontier AI while mitigating the most significant risks," the company said.
That mission is defined as: "The responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
"We do not pursue projects based on commercial opportunity or research novelty alone; our efforts must advance our mission. "

Such hypothetical benefits include progress in healthcare, like the development of bespoke treatments for illnesses and improved disease detection, tailored education and legal advice and making more efficient power grids and batteries.
Decades of scientific progress could be condensed into years, accelerating drug discovery, disease detection, and the delivery of personalized therapy.

Anthropic said AI could provide individually tailored education and expert financial and legal advice, advance power grids and battery design for greater efficiency and reliability and help the "developing world" build more technological capabilities.
"Ultimately, we believe frontier AI will help drive global economic growth," the company said.

articles.headline: Why Democrats are pivoting to thirst traps
keyFacts: Democratic candidates like Jon Ossoff and Abdul El-Sayed are becoming the subjects of organic online "thirst edits" and fan videos ahead of the 2026 midterms.
Grace Panetta of The 19th said that Democratic operatives and official accounts are leaning into this trend to win back ground on the internet after the 2024 election.
Panetta noted that while appearance-focused strategies carry risks of objectification, supporters and creators view them as a way to engage voters in an image-obsessed society.
body: “It is a very real dynamic that you could have all these videos about Jon Ossoff, and it's not seen as detracting away from his overall message or his seriousness as a politician,” The 19th’s Grace Panetta said on Vox’s Today, Explained podcast. | Elijah Nouvelage/Getty Images
Democrats have been emphasizing lots of issues in the runup to the 2026 midterms: The Iran war. The state of the economy and healthcare. Corruption. And…hotness.

Specifically, their candidates: The internet is awash in clips of Michigan candidate Abdul El-Sayed pumping iron and podcasters proclaiming that “America deserves a hot president” in a video interspersed with photos of Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff.

Having a good-looking candidate is by no means a new tactic — famously, it may have helped John F. Kennedy win election over Richard Nixon — but the online left is adapting that strategy for the internet and fandom age.

Grace Panetta, a politics reporter for The 19th, wrote about how “thirst edits” of Ossoff in particular are proliferating online. Panetta says the organic origins of a lot of these videos are of particular interest to Democratic operatives, who see it as a way to gain back ground they lost on the internet after the 2024 election.

Panetta spoke with Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram about who’s thirsting over Democratic politicians in the first place, how 2026’s hot candidates are different from those of yore, and whether it’s actually giving them a boost.

Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts , Pandora , and Spotify .
Where are these edits coming from?

Regular online creators. And it’s important to note at the outset that these are not paid partnerships. The campaign is not paying these influencers to make edits about how they think their candidate’s really attractive.
That’s partly why I wanted to dig into it, because it’s organic. These are just online creators wanting to draw visibility and attention to a candidate that they really like.
Jon Ossoff is currently running for reelection in these midterms. How do we know for sure that he isn’t somehow behind the campaign?

I spoke to several creators who make these videos and they said that they’re doing it for the love of the game and they’re just supporters. His campaign did not give me a quote or a statement for this story. So it’s fair to assume that he’s not directly involved and he doesn’t repost these videos.

But as people pointed out to me, his campaign knows that they have an attractive, compelling candidate. And they’ve previously been vaunted for their digital strategy this cycle of putting out very high-quality livestreams of his rallies. There’s a lot of material for an enterprising TikToker who wants to make these edits or clips. They have a lot to work with.
His campaign, as one person put it, is definitely playing into that, but not directly engaging. It’s a fine line to walk.
Is it just an Ossoff thing or is this going on with other candidates? I do recall that Abdul El-Sayed hits the gym.

Famously so. Yes, he hits the gym. I just watched so many videos for this story. I also came across a fair number of Gavin Newsom edits. There are people who think he gives sort of a Patrick Bateman, American Psycho vibe.

There are also official Democratic accounts, including the TikTok account for the DNC, the headquarters account, which was formerly Kamala HQ, who have been posting edits of Ossoff and also Abdul El-Sayed, who kind of leans into this gym-bro persona.
The headquarters account posted a side-by-side of Ossoff and Abdul El-Sayed with the caption, “There are 69 days until election day.”
Nice.

Yes. There are also lots of edits of Mamdani, and former President Barack Obama. Obama nostalgia content goes hard on the internet. So you’re seeing these more official side Democratic campaign accounts leaning into it and playing up their candidates.
Having an attractive candidate is nothing new. You mentioned Obama. JFK was famously dashing. What feels different about what you’re seeing now on social media?
I think this is really a culmination of a lot of different things happening right now in politics and specifically within the Democratic Party.

After their loss in 2024, there was a lot of conversation about the gerontocracy, how we’re governed by a lot of really old people, for the most part, in this century. And also about Democrats’ digital strategy and the aftermath of 2024.

One thing that a lot of people in that digital space have been talking about is how Republicans and the Trump campaign really capitalized on getting that organic engagement on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, where a lot of Americans are now going to get at least some of their news, and also engaging with and encouraging the creation of this kind of organic content on platforms and from creators that are not always expressly political or official-side.
“A candidate’s messaging strategy is only as good as the content and only if it meets people where they are and actually speaks to a real need people have.”

As one Democrat I talked to put it, she thinks it’s a way for Democrats to win back the internet and to really create a contrast with the Republicans. And she said to have fun on the internet because Republicans are having fun on the internet and it appears to be working for them, or at least it was in 2024.
Is there something about this being something on the left that makes it sort of tricky? This is, broadly speaking, objectification, right?
It is a fine line between thirst and objectification. And there is also a gendered element to it that it is mostly men that these types of videos are being made about.

Now, granted, a lot of people make sort of hype edits or positive content about AOC because she’s a very popular female politician on the left, but it’s true that women candidates are held to higher standards in terms of how they present themselves and how their supporters portray them.
It is a very real dynamic that you could have all these videos about Jon Ossoff, and it’s not seen as detracting away from his overall message or his seriousness as a politician.
Is there a drawback of focusing on looks? Does it make the Democratic Party or these candidates seem superficial or not that serious?

President Trump has been the defining figure in our politics for 10 years now. And he is famously very, very image focused and image obsessed. We live in a very image-obsessed society, and I think there’s kind of a bipartisan acknowledgement of that.

And looks matter to people in all kinds of ways. They do matter in politics, they do matter to voters. Whether you like that that’s the case or not, it is the reality. And I think the way that a lot of people on the left see this is, people want to look at attractive people. People take attractive people more seriously and are more willing to listen to them. So we should play into that and play that up.

That’s also been the case on the right. President Trump famously loves people out of “central casting.” There’s been this whole movement on the right about making conservatism sexy again. And especially at the beginning of the second Trump term, you had all these influencers talking about how the second Trump term was going to usher in this great age of hotness, which is of course very based on sort of stereotypical male-centered Eurocentric beauty standards.

I think the genie’s out of the bottle on this one in terms of the fact that our politics and society is very image-obsessed. And I think the left, being locked out of power, realizes they have to play on those terms and they have fun doing it.
You could look at it as giving “Kamala is brat,” which famously did not work. Is it working in any tangible way for Ossoff, for Abdul El-Sayed, or anyone else?

I think a lot of the time in politics, the success of a message is really dependent on the broader political situation. I think a part of the reason that the Kamala’s brat thing didn’t work is people were like, “Okay, that’s great, but my gas is too expensive and prices are too high and I’m not happy with how things have gone under the Biden administration, so I don’t really care.” I don’t know that specific digital strategy makes or breaks a campaign or candidate, but it feeds into a bunch of larger factors.

Something that a lot of people I spoke to said they liked about Jon Ossoff is how he is incredibly serious in Senate hearings. He doesn’t grandstand. He really holds Trump administration officials’ feet to the fire. He’s been very focused in his role in the Senate and on the campaign trail about calling out corruption. He’s a very, very gifted speaker and orator.

So I think a candidate’s messaging strategy is only as good as the content and only if it meets people where they are and actually speaks to a real need people have. And I think people are really unhappy with the second Trump term and politicians being super old and out of touch, and it’s a perfect storm of factors that makes it work for him.

articles.headline: Palworld's First Official Toy Collection Is Here, Complete With Mystery Eggs and Adorable Pals
keyFacts: Collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the first official Palworld toy collection.
The collection includes 4-inch articulated figures, 3-inch collector sets, and two different mystery egg products.
The toy collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon.
body: It's a good time to be a Palworld obsessive. The game recently teased its next update, Palworld: Side by Side , coming this winter, and now collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs. It's available now on Amazon .

Decorate your desk with the frankly adorable Chillet, take everyone's favorite oversized electric menace Grizzbolt out and about, and keep the perpetually vacant-looking Relaxasaurus in your pocket to remind you not to scream at your boss.

There are four different products in the collection, starting with a range of 4-inch articulated figures featuring Foxparks, Relaxasaurus, Grizzbolt, and Lifmunk. Each comes with its own Battle FX accessory, so you can make them fight without having to worry about a raid on your base.

For those who prefer their Pals a little smaller, because it's not the size of the Pal that matters but what you do with it that counts, there's also a 3-inch collector set featuring Chillet, Grizzbolt, and Relaxasaurus ( see at Amazon ).

And because apparently collecting Pals in the game wasn't enough, there are two different mystery collections to hunt down. The Cheebee Micro Blind Mystery Pal Egg 12-Pack includes a dozen 1.5-inch mystery figures, while the Blind Egg Incubator Reveal 8-Pack offers eight miniature Pals to hatch and collect.

As always, the blind-box format means there's no guarantee you'll get the Pal you're after, so happy hunting to all the completionists out there. At least these ones won't require you to craft hundreds of Pal Spheres.
The collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon .

articles.headline: Apple adds more Siri AI tools in its 27.2 system updates, out today
keyFacts: Apple released its 27.2 system updates, introducing new Siri AI tools such as past conversation recall and support for five additional languages.
The new Siri AI features are available on iPhone 16 models and later, along with the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max.
The 27.2 updates also bring general operating system improvements and device-specific additions for iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Vision Pro, HomePod, and watchOS.
body: Apple adds more Siri AI tools in its 27.2 system updates, out today
Siri now offers conversation recall and support for five more languages.

Apple has released new versions of its operating systems that bring additional Siri and AI functions to its hardware. On supported iPhone models, iOS 27.2 introduces the ability for Siri AI to recall past conversations the user has had with the chatbot. Today's iOS 27.2 update also adds more sources of information Siri can draw on. The AI tool can now pull information from more granular places, such as photos sent in Messages, attendees on Calendar invites and voicemails. An iPhone user can also opt to prevent Siri, Search and suggestions from accessing a particular program in the Excluded Apps setting. Users can now select and copy partial elements of responses from Siri AI with the addition of granular text selection. Finally, Apple has added language support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Those Siri AI features are available on all iPhone 16 models and later, as well as on the iPhone 15 Pro and the iPhone 15 Pro Max. All iPhones can take advantage of the other updates in iOS 27.2. Some of those new updates include support for editing captions and comments in Shared Albums in the Photos app, Suggestions in the Messages app for taking contextual actions based on texts, and support for Google's SynthID watermarking tool for identifying images created or modified with generative AI in Photos or Image Playground.

The iPhone Duo has a few dedicated changes in iOS 27.2. The first foldable iPhone now supports the Apple Pencil and use of Edge Light, a macOS feature that creates an on-screen ring light for video calls.

watchOS 27.2 is also getting the same Siri AI feature lineup as the iPhones, while macOS 27.2 includes the Siri AI updates for past conversation recall and Suggestions in Messages in addition to the usual bug fixes and security updates. Apple has also pushed the 27.2 updates for its iPad, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Homepod products today.

articles.headline: Man Utd players set to return to training with Carrick's future still uncertain
keyFacts: Manchester United players are set to return to training on Tuesday following a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.
Head coach Michael Carrick's future remains uncertain as club executives discuss next steps after an eight-game winless run.
Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met at the training base on Monday to consider the team's leadership.
body: Manchester United: Players to return to training on Tuesday but uncertain if Michael Carrick will be in charge

Man Utd beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick; captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and United are eight games without a win; players set to return to training on Tuesday after Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox met for talks on Monday
Monday 26 October 2026 20:13, UK
Manchester United's players are set to return to training at Carrington on Tuesday - but it is still uncertain whether Michael Carrick will be in charge.
United head coach Carrick was at Carrington on Monday to watch the club's U21s take on Hull in a behind-closed-doors game.

The first-team players had a scheduled day off but Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, director of football, also met at the training base, with their talks focused on next steps following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.
It remains to be seen what the United hierarchy, which includes Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the part-owner, will decide.

United's defeat to Bournemouth saw Carrick drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench after he questioned his tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss to Como. It extended United's winless run to eight games across all competitions.
Carrick has overseen United's worst start to a Premier League season. They are 16th in the table, with seven points from their seven games, and just one point adrift of the relegation zone.

Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season, following Ruben Amorim's sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.
Carrick was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Season and, in May, signed a new contract running to 2028.
How a 'strange day' at Carrington unfolded
Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan:

"It's been quite a bizarre, strange day at Carrington. This morning, we saw director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada arrive quite early. A few players were in receiving treatment on injuries. Captain Bruno Fernandes, Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko were all in.
"Michael Carrick arrived just before 2pm. From what we understand, he was here to watch the U21s take on Hull City.

"It paints quite an awkward picture. On one end of the car park at Carrington you have the academy building, where Carrick would have been watching the U21s' game, while on the other side you would have had Wilcox and Berrada discussing his future as well as what is the future of Man Utd, what are the next steps potentially in the head coach position.
"As far as we know, no talks between Carrick and Wilcox happened. It's quite tough when you look at the timeline because the game will have finished around 4pm.
"We saw Wilcox leave Carrington around 4.30pm. We understand Carrick left around 4.45pm. Would they have had talks today? It remains to be seen.
"Carrick's future remains in huge doubt and there's no further clarity on whether he will continue or not."
Why there hasn't been swift action on Carrick's future
Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:
"I thought this would happen pretty quickly. The fact it hasn't happened makes me think one of two things are going on.

"Probably the most likely is Man Utd's bosses are taking their time to consider who they want as a replacement. The worst-case scenario for Man Utd would be if they sacked Michael Carrick and the person they went for didn't want the job, or they couldn't agree a deal with them and they were left in limbo for days, possibly weeks.
"We know it happens in football all the time - clubs try to set up a replacement before they get rid of the incumbent.
"The second thing is they are very conscious - and it was made clear to them at Old Trafford - just how popular Michael Carrick is among the Man Utd support.
"The same thing happened with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021 - he gave the most incredible departure video, despite being sacked by Man Utd.

"The club wanted to make sure it ended amicably. I think Man Utd bosses are thinking the same thing here. There might not be an exit video from Carrick but they want this done humanely and respectfully.
"If they don't, the backlash from supporters could be even stronger."

articles.headline: Diablo 4’s War Plans Are Getting A Huge Upgrade In Season 16
keyFacts: Developer Blizzard announced that Diablo 4's War Plans system is receiving a major upgrade in Season 16.
The new War Plans Tactics system allows players to invest points to control activities and reward drops, according to Blizzard.
Diablo 4 Season 16 is scheduled to launch on December 1 after a public test realm period.
body: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over their endgame activities and rewards.

Developer Blizzard introduced War Plans earlier this year as part of the game's second (and last) expansion , Lord of Hatred. It's an endgame system where players can essentially create a playlist of endgame activities, along the way ranking up those activities via a skill tree to make them even more rewarding.

It was a welcome addition, but unfortunately only gave players minimal control over what activities would appear as part of their plans. Players could also only reroll their War Plans a limited number of times, meaning if you didn't like a particular activity, oftentimes you were stuck having to do it.

All of that looks to be changing in Season 16 with the addition of a new meta-progression system called War Plans Tactics. By completing War Plan activities, players will be able to invest points into the tactics tree to make it so certain activities are more likely to appear and specific types of rewards will drop. How players reroll their War Plans is also changing, with a new currency called Marks of Wisdom that will cap at 20 and should let players reroll their plans more often.

As detailed by Blizzard in a blog post ahead of the season arriving on the Diablo 4 public test realm October 27, players will be able to assign up to three points into each endgame activity and up to three points into different types of rewards.

"Earn points from completing War Plans activities, then invest these points into nodes to increase the chance of preferred activities or rewards appearing," Blizzard said. "This allows you to tailor your War Plans more closely with both your goals and playstyle."
A look at Diablo 4 Season 16's War Plans Tactics skill tree.

Putting at least one point into Helltides or Nightmare dungeons also grants the choice of increased chances for Greater Helltides and Escalation Nightmare dungeons, respectively. On the reward side, players will be able to make it so they are more likely to earn armor, weapons, jewelry, Obducite, salvage, gems, gold, activity keys, Horadric Cube materials, or Talisman items from activities.

The new tactics system isn't the only change coming to War Plans. A new seasonal War Plans tree, Tyrael's Boons, will also be coming with Season 16. There will be four Tyrael's Boons' paths to invest points into, with Blizzard stating players will be able to choose up to four of the six nodes within each path. Those four paths are:
Curious Addition: Upgrades the Purveyor of Curiosities to increase the chances for more and higher quality items.
Merchant of Mystery: Adds a new merchant in Torment difficulties that sell item caches in exchange for Forgotten Souls.
Scent of Gold: Increases the amount of gold, experience, and materials you earn.

Trash for Treasure: Reduces transmuting costs, increases chances to earn Obducite and salvage, and can even grant a new Horadric Cube recipe that allows players to upgrade a Tempered Affix on an item into a Greater Affix.

The changes to War Plans look to be the biggest features coming as part of Season 16, but there will additionally be a new type of gear to acquire, Horadric legendaries. These special legendaries will synergize with specific Talisman charms, with Horadric legendary jewelry items even counting for Talisman set bonuses. That should open the door to all kinds of new set and charm combinations that are sure to result in some wild new endgame builds.

Diablo 4 Season 16 will be playable on the PTR until November 3, with the full season set to launch December 1. Though Diablo 4 won't be getting additional expansions, it will get a new class, the Amazon , in the first half of next year.

As for what's next for the franchise, Diablo 5 is slated to arrive in 2029 . Blizzard has already revealed three of the game's playable classes and promised it will have more classes at launch than any previous Diablo game.

articles.headline: Player in Stokes and Atkinson altercation joins Bristol after Saracens sacking
keyFacts: Bristol Bears have signed forward Totoa Auvaa two weeks after Saracens sacked him following a police-investigated incident.
Auvaa was previously involved in a nightclub altercation with cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson and had disciplinary issues on the field.
Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam said the club will provide Auvaa with mentorship, guidance, and support to help him develop.
body: - Published
Bristol Bears have signed Samoan forward Totoa Auvaa, two weeks after he was sacked by Saracens.
Auvaa, 21, was involved in a nightclub altercation with England cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson in June.
He was let go by Sarries following another incident in St Albans, which police are investigating.
"His agent reached out to me to see if I would be willing to help him and give him a second chance," Bristol's director of rugby Pat Lam said.
"I've always believed that young people deserve the opportunity to learn from those experiences, grow and become better people."
Lam, himself a former Samoan international, told Bristol's website, external he believed the club could help provide support to Auvaa and was the right place for him to develop on and off the field.
"Totoa is a big, physical young man with enormous potential, who unfortunately has made some mistakes since arriving from a small village in Samoa to the massive city of London.

"Having spent time with Totoa, I feel confident that we can provide him with the mentorship, guidance, support and structure to give him the best possible opportunity to succeed, not just as a rugby player, but as a person - someone his parents and family all the way back in Samoa will be proud of."
Auvaa's disciplinary issues have not been restricted to late-night altercations.

While on loan at Championship club Ampthill last season, he was sent off twice for violent conduct - once, punching an opposition player in the face in the aftermath of conceding a try, and, in another match, kicking someone in the head at the bottom of a ruck.
Auvaa's youth, recent arrival in England and the stress of supporting his father through illness back home in Samoa were put forward in mitigation.

When he was involved in the nightclub incident with Atkinson and Stokes, in which a member of England's security staff was left bloodied after being struck by Auvaa, Saracens said they would stand by him.

However, after the incident in St Albans, the club said, external his conduct had fallen "short of the standards expected of everyone who represents Saracens, both on and off the pitch" and he was sacked.
A statement issued by Hertfordshire Police on the incident said: "Police are investigating an altercation which occurred between 0215 and 0220 on Sunday [11 October] in St Peter's Street, St Albans.
"It is alleged a man aged in his twenties was approached by another man who then punched him to the face. Enquiries are ongoing at this time."
Auvaa made one appearance for Saracens, playing 20 minutes of a Prem Rugby Cup match in September.

articles.headline: iPhone Duo now supports Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2
keyFacts: Apple released iOS 27.2, which adds Apple Pencil support and an Edge Light feature to the iPhone Duo.
The software update introduces Siri AI action suggestions in Messages and expands Siri AI language support.
Apple also released updates for macOS, watchOS, visionOS, tvOS, and HomePod alongside iOS 27.2.
body: Apple has just released iOS 27.2, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The software update also includes an “Edge Light” feature for the iPhone Duo that’s intended to illuminate your face during video calls.
iPhone Duo now supports Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2
The latest iOS update also adds dual-camera use in group FaceTime calls.

Apple previously said the iPhone Duo would add support for the Apple Pencil “later this year.” The company’s first foldable comes with revamped iOS 27 controls designed to work across the device’s 7.6-inch inner display and 5.4-inch outer screen. Many major apps, like Netflix, Prime Video, and Microsoft Outlook, already support the Duo’s extra screen real estate, but some still need some work.

The iOS 27.2 update also allows Siri AI to take suggested actions in Messages, while adding support for Siri AI in more languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Apple is rolling out support for Google’s SynthID AI watermark in Photos and Image Playground, too, according to 9to5Mac.

Other smaller but notable updates include user profiles on the Apple TV app on iPhone. The Apple Podcasts app is also replacing its “Up Next” queue with a list of “New Episodes,” along with a “Continue Playing” section just beneath it. You’ll also see the new Apple Music logo. And group calls on FaceTime now support dual capture so you can show both what’s visible from your selfie cam and your back cameras.
Apple also released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2.

articles.headline: Boston Dynamics employees want to block sale of robot dogs to ICE
keyFacts: Over 300 Boston Dynamics employees signed a petition asking executives to halt the sale of robot dogs to ICE.
Executives stood by the deal, stating that the modified robots would not be weaponized and were intended for safety and inspection missions.
The Department of Homeland Security awarded a $1.3 million contract to provide ICE with four modified Boston Dynamics robots.
body: Hundreds of employees at the US robotics firm Boston Dynamics signed a petition calling for executives to halt a sale of the company’s robot dogs to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement—but executives stood by the deal, while saying the robots would not be weaponized.

On September 25, the Department of Homeland Security contract awarded $1.3 million to a Connecticut company called Radeco to provide ICE with modified versions of Boston Dynamics’ quadruped robots. But Boston Dynamics workers sent the petition letter with more than 300 signatures—half of them anonymous—to the company’s executives in early September and shared copies with The Boston Globe and WBUR public radio station.

“Many of us have gotten messages from friends and family, asking us in disbelief and horror if this news is true, and how we can live with ourselves if it is,” according to the petition. “The risk for Boston Dynamics is simply too great to continue with this deal.”

The petition described the signatories as employees who normally “love showing off what we do to our friends, family and the world” and who “love challenging ourselves to innovate and change the perception of what robots can do.” The 300 signatures come out of a total Boston Dynamics workforce of approximately 1,400 people.
Spot’s Cerberus upgrade

The ICE contract covers the purchase of four Boston Dynamics Spot robots that were modified by Radeco to be marketed as a robot platform named Cerberus. The contract describes these Cerberus robots as being intended to “detect radiation, toxic gas leaks and explosive threats in urban environments or disaster zones,” along with enabling other remote observation and inspection missions.

A centerpiece of the upgraded robot is an oxygen sensor that is intended to “ensure the air quality is breathable when personnel are placed in confined spaces such as tunnels.” The Cerberus robot dog also has a camera equipped with 30-times zoom capability, 360-degree cameras, and infrared thermal imaging.

articles.headline: Microsoft releases emergency .NET security fixes for Google Brotli bug
keyFacts: Microsoft urged .NET users to update immediately after releasing emergency security fixes for a vulnerability in Google's Brotli compression technology.
Senior program manager Rahul Bhandari stated that the buffer overflow flaw could allow unauthenticated attackers to corrupt process memory or cause a denial of service.
OpenAI recommended blocking untrusted Brotli-compressed data and rebuilding affected deployments until patches can be applied.
body: To address a vulnerability in Google's Brotli compression technology that could allow attackers to corrupt process memory, Microsoft is urging .NET users to update "as soon as possible" after releasing an out-of-band (OOB) security update.
It released new versions for .NET 8, 9, 10, and .NET 11 to patch against the Brotli bug, following similar updates from Node.js, Python, and other projects.

Senior program manager Rahul Bhandari said in the October 25 release that the buffer overflow vulnerability in Brotli, tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and rated 8.1 under CVSS v3.1 in Microsoft's advisory, could allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory, potentially resulting in information disclosure, denial of service, or elevation of privilege.

Microsoft’s own advisory for the vulnerability, which some are referring to as Broccoli2Shell or Node2Shell, confirms that while experts have cobbled working exploits together , there is nothing to suggest that criminals are using them in successful attacks.
However, its exploitability assessment reads: “Exploitation More Likely.”
Broccoli2Shell was first disclosed on October 21 by the Node.js team, which released fixes for ten vulnerabilities, the most serious of which was CVE-2026-111497.

Node.js credited Khai Tran and Sylvie Mayer of OpenAI’s Codex Security with the discovery, but failed to mention why it was only recognized as a security flaw and disclosed properly in October, despite the underlying bug having been fixed in Brotli's source code in February.

OpenAI filled in the gap with a Xeet : “This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability, and there was no more recent release of Brotli.
“Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software.”
Attackers can exploit vulnerable systems by providing them with malicious Brotli-compressed data via a specially crafted request.

The vulnerability went slightly under the radar due to the disclosure timing closely aligning with that of PHP2Shell , although fixing the critical flaw should be a priority due to the range of technologies that are affected.

In addition to .NET, Node.js, and Python, Bun , Envoy , and Istio have all released patches, and JFrog has worked up an exploit affecting FFmpeg using a specially crafted JPEG XL image, extending the exploit path beyond HTTP.
It said that FFmpeg reaches Brotli through libjxl, which it uses to decompress metadata stored in brob boxes within the image format.
The same researchers said the vulnerability affects Apache Arrow too, with attackers able to cause a denial of service.

Merav Bar, threat researcher at Wiz, added that cloud users are exposed extensively, noting that 91 percent of cloud environments rely on components vulnerable to the Brotli flaw and that 82 percent of cloud environments have publicly exposed Node.js instances.

She said : “Cloud environments are particularly exposed due to the widespread use of Brotli-enabled components across containerized applications, Kubernetes clusters, API gateways, reverse proxies, serverless workloads, and cloud-hosted web services.”

“Successful exploitation could enable attackers to compromise application workloads, access sensitive information, disrupt service availability, or execute malicious code within affected containers or runtime environments,” Bar added.

In an advisory published through its Patch the Planet initiative, OpenAI recommended blocking untrusted Brotli-compressed data where practical until patches can be applied. It also advised maintainers to rebuild affected deployments and restart services to ensure the fixes take effect. ®

articles.headline: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban
keyFacts: An Australian judge rejected a life-sentenced prisoner's human rights challenge against a state prison ban on Vegemite.
Inmate Andre McKechnie argued that withholding Vegemite breached his right to enjoy his culture as an Australian.
Justice Claire Harris ruled the ban was justified after prison officials testified Vegemite could hinder drug dogs and help brew alcohol.
body: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban

MELBOURNE, Australia — A prisoner on Monday lost his challenge to an Australian state's ban on inmates eating Vegemite after he argued in court that withholding the polarizing yeast-based spread breached his human right to "enjoy his culture as an Australian."
Andre McKechnie, 55, who is serving a life sentence for murder, took his battle for the salty, sticky, black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the Supreme Court of the state of Victoria last year.

He had argued being refused Vegemite denied him his right under the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act to "enjoy his culture as an Australian in the community with other persons of Australian background," court documents showed.
Justice Claire Harris accepted prison authorities' refusal to allow McKechnie Vegemite "limited his cultural rights" under the charter.
But she found the ban was justified in meeting authorities' goals of removing illicit drugs and alcohol from the prison system.
"The limitation on Mr. McKechnie's ability to enjoy Vegemite in community with other persons of Australian background is primarily that he is a prisoner," Harris wrote in her 47-page judgment.
Prison officials testify Vegemite could impair drug sniffer dogs and be used to make alcohol

Prison officials testified at a trial in July that Vegemite had been banned throughout the state's 12 prisons for the past 20 years because it could potentially impair sniffer dogs' ability to detect narcotics and could be used to brew alcohol because of its yeast content.

McKechnie, who represented himself in court by video link from maximum security Barwon Prison west of Melbourne, argued that the fact that neighboring New South Wales state did not ban Vegemite from its prisons was evidence that there were "less restrictive means reasonably available" to achieve such drug and alcohol outcomes.

Most Australians revere Vegemite as an unfairly maligned culinary icon, and more than 80% of Australian households are estimated to have a jar in their pantries. Vegemite is typically considered an acquired taste at best by those who weren't raised on it.
The last U.S. president to visit Australia, Barack Obama, once said: "It's horrible."
Prisoner argues Vegemite ban contributed to vitamin deficiency
McKechnie had initially testified that the lack of Vegemite had contributed to his thiamine deficiency.
He said both Vegemite and pork were sources of thiamine, also known as vitamin B1. As a Jew who observed kosher law, he told the court he couldn't eat pork either and took daily doses of the vitamin.
Vegemite has long been marketed as a source of B vitamins thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2), niacin (B3) and folate (B9) which are promoted as healthy additions to the diets of growing children.
But McKechnie dropped the thiamine issue as "not important," after lawyers for the prison authorities objected to his evidence.
Prisoner said Vegemite ban left him feeling 'deprived, sad and disconnected'
McKechnie said not eating Vegemite made him feel "deprived of being able to practice my Australian culture, sad and disconnected from my family and community."

The judge responded that "it is difficult to accept that the inability to consume Vegemite, rather than the fact of his imprisonment, is a material cause of his sadness and disconnection from his family and community."
McKechnie cited an article published in the food studies journal "Gastronomica" in 2003 that said, "Vegemite may be the best predictor of national identity of any food in the world."
The article, based on research by Australia's Queensland University in 1995, found that a "taste for the spread strongly correlates with early exposure and to Australian birth and ancestry."
McKechnie also referred to the Australian Olympic Committee overturning an Chinese import ban on Vegemite ahead of the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing.
He cited Australian band Men at Work's 1980s international hit "Down Under" that mentions a "Vegemite sandwich."

On the effectiveness of smearing contraband with Vegemite, McKechnie cited a Melbourne newspaper article from 2017 that reported a man's unsuccessful attempt to use the odor of the spread to conceal illicit drugs that he attempted to smuggle into a music festival in Victoria. The attempt was thwarted by police sniffer dogs.
Judge rejects evidence that Vegemite doesn't interfere with drug sniffer dogs
The judge upheld prison authorities' argument that McKechnie had failed to provide any proper foundations for his opinion that Vegemite does not interfere with drug sniffer dogs.
McKechnie also argued that Vegemite contained "no live yeast" and that any piece of fruit would be more useful in making alcohol than the spread.
A state prison department manager, Kevin White, cited publicly available research that said Vegemite helped home-brewed beer ferment more quickly.
Vegemite's owner, Bega Group, did not respond to a request for comment on Monday.
